title: Ketamine Attenuates TNF-α-Induced Blood-Brain Barrier Damage and Neuroinflammation in Association with NF-κB Pathway.
abstract: Systemic inflammatory response syndrome is a complex clinical syndrome driven by dysregulated inflammatory cascades, and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) acts as a core upstream mediator in its pathogenesis. In this study, we established a mouse model of acute TNF-α-induced systemic inflammatory brain injury via a single tail vein injection of TNF-α. Ketamine (KET) (20mg/kg) was administered intraperitoneally 20min prior to the insult, and phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA), a protein kinase C activator that can indirectly trigger nuclear factor-κB p65 (NF-κB) pathway activation, was applied in vivo for pharmacological validation. In vivo, behavioral performance, neuronal histopathological damage, blood-brain barrier (BBB) structural and functional integrity, and microglial activation were evaluated; in vitro, inflammatory responses were assessed in TNF-α-stimulated BV2 microglia. KET pretreatment significantly alleviated TNF-α-induced behavioral deficits, mitigated neuronal damage and preserved Nissl body integrity, maintained the continuity of tight junction proteins in cerebrovascular endothelium, reduced BBB permeability, and suppressed microglial overactivation and pro-inflammatory mediator expression. Mechanistically, KET inhibited NF-κB p65 nuclear translocation in both cerebrovascular endothelium and microglia and downregulated endothelial matrix metalloproteinase-9; these effects were partially reversed by PMA co-treatment. Collectively, prophylactic KET administration exerts BBB-protective and anti-neuroinflammatory effects in association with NF-κB pathway inhibition, providing preclinical evidence for the prevention of inflammatory brain injury in the context of systemic TNF-α elevation.

title: EEG Microstate Alterations and Their Association with Cognitive Performance in Late-Onset Epilepsy of Unknown Etiology: Comparison with Alzheimer's Disease.
abstract: Cognitive impairment is common in late-onset epilepsy of unknown etiology (LOEU), but its electrophysiological correlates and relationship to Alzheimer's disease (AD) remain unclear. We compared resting-state electroencephalogram (EEG) microstate dynamics among LOEU, AD, and cognitively normal (CN) groups and examined their associations with cognitive performance. Eyes-closed 32-channel resting-state EEG recordings were analyzed from 60 patients with LOEU, 65 with AD, and 60 CN participants. Four canonical microstate classes (A-D) were identified. Group differences in microstate parameters were tested with false discovery rate correction. Associations with Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) and Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores were examined using multivariable interaction models adjusted for age, sex, education, and cerebral small vessel disease burden. Microstate B duration was longer in LOEU and AD than in CN (Holm-adjusted p=0.011 and 0.016), whereas microstate C occurrence was lower in both patient groups (p=0.001 and 0.018). Microstate D duration was longer in LOEU than in CN and AD (both p=0.038). For microstate A duration, the group interaction survived false discovery rate correction for MMSE (q=0.0255) but not MoCA (q=0.122). In LOEU, longer microstate A duration was associated with lower MoCA and MMSE scores. Pairwise slope comparisons were more negative in LOEU than in CN for both outcomes, whereas LOEU-AD slope differences were not significant. LOEU showed altered resting-state EEG microstate dynamics that partly overlapped with those observed in AD, alongside a group difference in microstate D duration. Microstate A duration was associated with cognitive performance in LOEU, although this association did not significantly differ from that observed in AD. These findings support further investigation of EEG microstates as electrophysiological correlates of cognitive dysfunction in LOEU while also highlighting overlap with AD.

title: The conversion of pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells to eosinophil-like cells exacerbates the progression of pulmonary arterial hypertension with increased secretion of 12-HETE.
abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is characterised by progressive pulmonary arterial (PA) vascular remodeling, with abnormal phenotypic transformation of pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs) playing a central role. Arachidonic acid (AA) metabolites have been implicated in this process, yet the underlying cellular and molecular mechanisms by which its metabolite 12-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (12-HETE) contributes to PAH remain incompletely understood. Plasma concentrations of 12-HETE were significantly elevated in PAH patients. In SU5416/hypoxia (SuHx)-induced PAH mouse model, the 12/15-lipoxygenase (12/15-LOX) inhibitor ML-351 markedly attenuated disease progression. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis revealed a unrecognized phenotypic transdifferentiation of a subset of PASMCs into eosinophil-like (Eos-like) cells. Mechanistically, studies utilizing EOS-deficient (ΔdblGATA) mice demonstrated that these newly Eos-like cells, along with native eosinophils (EOS), secrete 12-HETE. In vitro CCK-8 assays confirmed that hypoxia-induced PASMC proliferation was attenuated by the leukotriene B4 receptor 2 (BLT2) antagonist LY255283, confirming that the 12-HETE/BLT2 axis drives PASMC proliferation, thereby creating a positive feedback loop that amplifies vascular remodeling. These findings establish the 12-HETE as a critical mediator of a novel EOS-PASMC signaling axis that drives PA vascular remodeling in PAH. This study highlights a promising new therapeutic strategy for PAH.

title: Effects of N-acetylcysteine administration on anxiety and hedonic-like behaviours, neuroendocrine and redox-related dysfunctions induced by two-hit stress exposure in male and female rats.
abstract: Early life stress may reshape the response to later adverse events. Animal models of prenatal stress (PNS) represent tools to unravel underpinning mechanisms, among which redox imbalance and neuroendocrine dysfunctions play a crucial role. Here, we investigated the effects of a chronic administration with the antioxidant compound N-Acetylcysteine (NAC) on a two-hit stress exposure paradigm in male and female rats, i.e. PNS (by maternal restraint-first hit), combined with social isolation during adolescence (second hit). Hedonic and anxiety-like behaviours were assessed by Sucrose Preference and Elevated Plus Maze (EPM) tests. Plasmatic levels of ROS, malondialdehyde, oxytocin and corticosterone were quantified, together with hypothalamic corticotropin-releasing factor. Moreover, activities of antioxidant enzymes superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase and glutathione peroxidase (GPx) were also assessed. PNS-exposed males and females exhibited an increased hedonic response, regardless of the second hit. Decreased time spent in the EPM open arms in both PNS-grouped and PNS-isolated males and females was detected, counterbalanced by NAC treatment only in females. CRF and ROS levels were increased in two-hit stress-exposed males and females, with a NAC-induced reduction. Oxytocin content, decreased in females following PNS and PNS-ISO exposure, was restored by NAC in PNS-ISO group. Weaker SOD and CAT activities, together with an enhancement of the GPx, were observed in two-hit exposed males and females, with NAC treatment determining their upregulation. Our data showed that PNS modulates the vulnerability to a second stress during adolescence, highlighting the pivotal role of early-life fetal programming. Furthermore, NAC represents a promising antioxidant compound targeting stress-induced dysfunctions.

title: Computer vision-aided locomotor behavioral analysis identifies therapeutic motor signatures in a mouse model of Huntington's disease.
abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive motor dysfunction. Traditional open-field tests quantify spontaneous locomotor parameters but provide limited information on the duration and sequencing of individual movements across HD stages. Here, we applied a computer vision-aided behavioral flow analysis to quantify fine, HD-relevant motor dysfunction in the zQ175DN HD mouse model, from early to developed HD motor deficits. With DeepLabCut-tracked body movements, Keypoint-MoSeq identified recurrent behavioral syllables through unsupervised segmentation of standard top-view open-field recordings. These syllables were then grouped into behavioral clusters and analyzed for transitions between movements. Disease stage-dependent syllable occurrence and transition structure changes were identified. Genotype classification using syllable mean duration showed insufficient discrimination at 6 months and modest discrimination at 9 months, and combined behavioral features yielded higher discrimination at 12 months. HD was also associated with changes in which behavioral clusters served as hubs in the transition networks and the probabilities of switching between behaviors. We integrated these features into an HD motor dysfunction (HDMD) score based on deviations from age-matched wild-type (WT) reference values. The HDMD score distinguished zQ175DN mice from WT at multiple HD stages and aligned with HD pathology and disease severity. This HDMD scoring system may support retrospective analysis and more efficient preclinical drug-study design, as suggested by preliminary effect-size and power estimates assuming partial normalization of the HD phenotype. Overall, the HDMD score summarizes subtle motor abnormalities in HD mice and indicates further validation for preclinical drug efficacy assessment.

title: Spatial-Frequency-Dependent Temporal Dynamics of Orientation Ensemble Representation.
abstract: Average representation refers to the rapid extraction of the central tendency from a set of stimuli by the visual system. However, whether this efficient process relies on specific spatial frequency (SF) information remains poorly understood. To investigate the roles of low spatial frequency (LSF) and high spatial frequency (HSF) information in orientation ensemble averaging and the underlying temporal dynamics, we conducted two experiments combining behavioral and electroencephalographic (EEG) measures. Experiment 1 examined the effects of SF and visual field location on mean orientation judgments. Behavioral results indicated that LSF ensembles yielded superior accuracy and shorter reaction times compared to HSF ensembles, with performance further enhanced in the peripheral versus central visual field. To characterize the underlying temporal dynamics of ensemble processing, Experiment 2 focused on the peripheral field and utilized a neural adaptation paradigm in which the adapted and control test ensembles were matched in numerosity and spatial configuration. Electrophysiological results revealed a sequential processing trajectory: the LSF condition initially elicited a significant neural adaptation effect at the early C1 stage, followed by an HSF-elicited adaptation effect at the P1 stage. Finally, at the late P3 stage, the LSF condition exhibited a repetition enhancement effect. These findings suggest that orientation ensemble representation follows a spatial-frequency-dependent, coarse-fine-refine multistage dynamic pattern. Specifically, early LSF information facilitates a rapid, coarse holistic estimate; subsequently, HSF information contributes fine-grained details; and ultimately, the representation may be refined or calibrated through a late-stage process that may involve updating early LSF-based predictions.

title: Capturing the patient journey of recent mothers at risk of postnatal depression: proof of concept of a weekly diary study.
abstract: Postnatal depression (PD) is a significant mental health issue affecting recent mothers worldwide, yet many do not seek professional help due to stigma, practical barriers, or the normalisation of distress. This study aimed to explore the help-seeking behaviour of recent mothers at risk of PD in Belgium, focusing on their access to and experiences with care, as well as the role of their social support networks. Additionally, we evaluated the feasibility of using weekly diary entries to longitudinally map patient journeys. A proof-of-concept study with a qualitative patient journey mapping approach was conducted. Five recent mothers at risk of PD were recruited via midwifery practises and social media. Participants completed a baseline questionnaire and weekly diaries for 12 weeks, detailing their emotional well-being, help-seeking behaviour, and healthcare interactions. Data were analysed through an inductive approach, and patient journey maps were created to visualise individual experiences. Participants sought help in approximately half of their emotionally challenging moments, with an equal preference for consulting healthcare professionals or turning to their social networks. Psychologists were the most frequently consulted professionals, and accessibility to care was generally rated as good. Key barriers to seeking professional help included a preference for self-reliance, doubts about treatment effectiveness, and the minimization of symptoms. Stigma and financial constraints were not significant barriers in this sample. The use of weekly diaries successfully captured longitudinal patient experiences and facilitated the creation of structured patient journey maps. Recent mothers at risk of PD demonstrate a mixed reliance on professional and social support systems, with primary care services being the most frequently accessed. The study also highlights the potential of weekly diaries for tracking patient experiences over time. Further research with a larger sample size and complementary interviews is recommended to enhance the understanding of PD-related help-seeking behaviours.

title: Describing the pre-moyamoya stage: Lesion distribution, disease progression, and the impact of RNF213.
abstract: Stenosis at the terminal portion of the internal carotid artery (ICA) is a characteristic feature of moyamoya disease (MMD). However, MMD may develop in patients with initially preserved terminal ICAs, and the lesion distribution and predictors of progression during the pre-moyamoya stage remain poorly defined. We conducted a single-center retrospective longitudinal cohort study of consecutive patients with intracranial arterial stenosis (ICAS) in the anterior circulation to characterize the pre-moyamoya stage of MMD, including the distribution of initial lesions and predictors of progression. Clinical, angiographic, and genetic data were analyzed. Among 624 patients with ICAS, 458 were diagnosed with MMD at the last follow-up. Of these, 33 patients with bilaterally preserved terminal ICAs subsequently progressed to MMD over a median interval of 55.3 months (IQR, 12.5-97.3), representing 7.2% of all MMD cases. Among the 66 hemispheres in patients with MMD progression, M1 stenosis was the most common initial lesion (54.5%), followed by A1 (12.1%) and C2 stenosis (7.6%). RNF213 p.R4810K genotyping was performed in 304 patients, of whom 74.0% harbored the mutation. Multivariable Cox regression analysis showed that the RNF213 p.R4810K mutation (HR, 20.2; 95% CI, 2.63-155; P = 0.004) and younger age (HR per 1-year increase, 0.953; 95% CI, 0.931-0.975; P < 0.001) were independently associated with progression to MMD. The pre-moyamoya stage is characterized by heterogeneous stenotic patterns, with M1 steno-occlusive lesions representing the most common initial manifestation. RNF213 p.R4810K genotyping may help identify patients at increased risk of progression to MMD.

title: Time for functional complement biomarkers in generalized Myasthenia Gravis.
Profiles and development of repetitive behavior in children with different genetic subtypes of Prader-Willi syndrome.
abstract: Prader-Willi Syndrome (PWS) is associated with a broad behavioral phenotype, including repetitive behaviors and restricted interests (RBRI), such as hoarding, skin-picking, and repetitive questioning. We examined RBRI in PWS probands (n = 110) and a typically-developing (TD) cohort (n = 1428), across three age groups, on a multidimensional measure assessing three aspects of RBRI: including Total RBRI, Rigidity/Insistence on Sameness, and Repetitive Motor Behaviors/Compulsions. We also compared PWS genetic subtypes (paternal deletions, maternal uniparental disomy), and Types I and II deletion cases to each other, and to the TD group. Finally, in PWS participants, we explored the shared variance between RBRI factors and adaptive and maladaptive behaviors associated with PWS. Caregivers completed the CRI-R (assessing RBRI), the PADQ (anxiousness), and SDQ (strengths and difficulties questionnaire). The PWS group exhibited more RBRI overall than the TD group. However, these group differences varied by Age Group such that RBRI scores became increasingly divergent at the oldest age cohort - particularly for the PWS mUPD group. Finally, anxiousness predicted variance in RBRI for both the DEL and mUPD groups, with Emotional Problems adding additional variance for the deletion group only. These findings speak to the differences in the profiles of RBRI in PWS genetic subtypes, as well as the developmental course of RBRI that may inform clinical intervention.

title: Design, synthesis and biological evaluation of novel vicinal diarylpyrazole- benzylpiperidine/carbamate hybrids as MAO-B inhibitors.
abstract: We report the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of two distinct series of vicinal diaryl pyrazole-based hybrids incorporating benzylpiperidine (37-67) and carbamate (68-91) moieties as multifunctional agents for Alzheimer's disease. All compounds were evaluated for in vitro monoamine oxidase-B (MAO-B) inhibition, with initial screening at 10 μM showing >90% inhibition for the majority of compounds. Compounds (42 and 90) were identified as potent MAO-B inhibitors, with IC₅₀ values of 109.3 ± 20.78 and 92.86 ± 7.66 nM, respectively. Structure-activity relationship analysis revealed that unsubstituted aryl groups at the C-3,4 positions of the pyrazole core were the most potent, followed by methoxy and chloro substitutions, while bulky substituents reduced potency. Carbamate derivatives (68-91) exhibited improved MAO-B inhibition relative to benzylpiperidine analogues (37-67), with phenyl and benzyl carbamate substitutions being most favorable. The compounds showed moderate acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibition, with compounds (83 and 90) displaying 89.5% and 94.7% inhibition at 10 μM, respectively. Compounds (42 and 90) also demonstrated low neurotoxicity in STHdhQ7/Q7 neuronal cells (MTT assay) and exhibited effective chelation of Zn2+, Cu2+, and Fe2+ ions. Molecular docking studies supported these findings, revealing key interactions within the MAO-B and AChE active sites. These results identify vicinal diaryl pyrazole-based hybrids, particularly compound (90) containing carbamate moiety, as promising multifunctional leads for further development as anti-Alzheimer agents.

title: Influence of bromine on the amoebicidal activity of cyclolauranes.
abstract: Primary amoebic meningoencephalitis, caused by Naegleria fowleri, is a rapidly fatal infection of the central nervous system for which no consistently effective treatment exists. Marine-derived halogenated sesquiterpenes represent a structurally promising class of antiparasitic leads, yet systematic structure-activity relationship (SAR) data within this series remain scarce. In this study, the antiparasitic activity of laurinterol (1) and its congeners bromolaurinterol (2) and debromolaurinterol (3), isolated from the red alga Laurencia johnstonii, was evaluated against trophozoites (compounds 1-3) and cysts (compounds 1 and 2) of two clinical isolates of N. fowleri (ATCC® 30808™ and 30215™). Laurinterol (1) exhibited low-micromolar anti-trophozoidal activity (IC₅₀ = 1.77 ± 0.28 μM and 4.28 ± 1 μM against ATCC® 30808™ and 30215™, respectively) and cysticidal potency (IC₅₀ = 0.98 ± 0.33 μM and 1.87 ± 0.61 μM) that is 16- to 20-fold higher than that of miltefosine, with laurinterol (1) selectivity indices of 88.3 and 36.5 against murine macrophages (J774A.1). The additional ortho‑bromine in bromolaurinterol (2) reduced activity approximately 4- to 9-fold across the endpoints evaluated, suggesting that di-ortho bromination is detrimental within this limited series of three natural congeners. The compounds induced a convergent cell-death marker profile in treated trophozoites, characterised by chromatin condensation, plasma membrane permeabilisation, mitochondrial depolarisation, reduced ATP content and increased ROS, consistent, in the case of laurinterol, with our previous evidence of Na+-ATPase inhibition. In silico ADME predictions suggested that these molecules may be blood-brain barrier-permeant, a possible pharmacokinetic advantage over amphotericin B that remains to be tested experimentally. Collectively, these in vitro data identify laurinterol (1) as a promising lead for further anti-N. fowleri drug development.

title: Psychometric validation of the Spanish version of the Huntington's Disease Health-Related Quality of Life Questionnaire (HDQoL©).
abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by motor, cognitive, and behavioural symptoms that substantially impair health-related quality of life (HRQoL). The Huntington Disease Health-Related Quality of Life questionnaire (HDQoL©) is a disease-specific instrument recommended for HRQoL assessment in HD; however, it has not been validated in the Spanish population. To evaluate the validity and reliability of the Spanish version of the HDQoL© in individuals with Huntington's disease in Spain. A multicentre, observational, cross-sectional validation study was conducted in neurology departments of 11 tertiary hospitals in Spain. Adults with genetically confirmed pathogenic HTT CAG expansion complete the authorized Spanish-language version of the HDQoL© together with the Unified Huntington's Disease Rating Scale (UHDRS), Stroop test, Problem Behaviors Assessment-short form (PBA-s), and SF-36. Psychometric analyses included exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, convergent and known-groups validity, internal consistency, and 4-week test-retest reliability. A total of 135 participants completed the baseline assessment, and 102 completed the retest. Factor analyses supported a five-domain, 33-item structure, explaining 69.0% of the variance, with good model fit (CFI = 0.957; TLI = 0.953; RMSEA = 0.076). HDQoL© domains showed significant correlations with relevant clinical, functional, cognitive, psychiatric, and HRQoL measures. Internal consistency ranged from α = 0.736-0.938, and test-retest reliability was good for four domains (ICC > 0.75). The Spanish version of the HDQoL© is a valid and reliable instrument for assessing HRQoL in individuals with HD in Spain.

title: Shared and subtype-specific lipidomic signatures precede ischemic stroke and intracerebral hemorrhage.
abstract: Altered redox homeostasis is increasingly recognized as an important contributor to cerebrovascular injury in stroke, yet relevant prospective population-based evidence on pre-diagnostic lipid remodeling remains limited. We aimed to characterize shared and subtype-divergent lipidomic signatures preceding ischemic stroke (IS) and intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). Within a nested case-control design in the Taizhou Longitudinal Study, 1103 incident IS cases, 159 incident ICH cases, and 1277 matched controls underwent high-coverage lipidomic profiling (1067 species across 37 subclasses). We identified a shared lipid signature across IS and ICH characterized by elevated acylcarnitines and sphingosine-1-phosphates and reduced phosphatidylserines and phosphatidylethanolamine plasmalogens. We further found that lipid structural features, including higher unsaturation and longer acyl-chain length in some lipid subclasses, were associated with increased stroke risk, whereas higher plasmalogen proportion was inversely associated. In contrast, neutral lipids showed subtype-specific patterns. Triacylglycerols (TAGs) and free fatty acids (FFAs) were broadly associated with IS risk, whereas predominantly very-long-chain species were linked to ICH. Network analysis supported divergent remodeling, showing altered TAG-FFA-acylcarnitine correlations in IS and reduced plasmalogen connectivity in ICH. Moreover, we developed subtype-specific lipid scores that showed promising discriminatory performance in internal validation. For IS, the AUCs were 0.63 (0.59-0.68) for the clinical model, 0.88 (0.85-0.90) for the lipid model, and 0.89 (0.86-0.91) for the combined model. The corresponding AUCs for ICH were 0.65 (0.55-0.75), 0.82 (0.75-0.87), and 0.86 (0.79-0.91), respectively. In an independent temporal validation, the AUCs were 0.60 (0.56-0.64), 0.76 (0.72-0.79), and 0.77 (0.73-0.80) for the clinical, lipid, and combined model of IS, and 0.62 (0.51-0.73), 0.72 (0.63-0.80), and 0.81 (0.75-0.87) for those of ICH, respectively. In conclusion, these findings identify shared and subtype-divergent lipidomic signatures preceding IS and ICH, with potential relevance to redox homeostasis.

title: Ultrasonography assessment of adnexal masses: how to predict malignancy.
journal: Best practice & research. Clinical obstetrics & gynaecology
abstract: Adnexal masses are frequently encountered in gynecological practice, and the primary clinical challenge is to estimate the likelihood of malignancy in order to guide appropriate patient management. Transvaginal ultrasonography is the first-line imaging modality and, in expert hands, a highly accurate technique for characterizing adnexal lesions, with magnetic resonance imaging serving as a complementary second-line test for sonographically indeterminate masses. This review provides a practical overview of contemporary ultrasound assessment of adnexal masses, focusing on the sonographic features associated with benign and malignant tumors, standardized terminology, and validated risk prediction models. We summarize the International Ovarian Tumor Analysis (IOTA) terminology and discuss the principal ultrasound-based approaches for risk stratification, including the IOTA Simple Rules, the Simple Rules Risk score, the Assessment of Different NEoplasias in the adneXa (ADNEX) model, and the benign-descriptors two-step strategy, together with their integration into the Ovarian-Adnexal Reporting and Data System (O-RADS). The review also examines the ultrasound characteristics that may help distinguish primary ovarian malignancies from metastatic lesions, emphasizing features that support differential diagnosis and appropriate referral. Current evidence indicates that standardized ultrasound assessment, combined with validated prediction models, provides an accurate and reproducible estimation of malignancy risk while complementing expert subjective evaluation. The ADNEX model offers the additional advantage of estimating the probability of different malignant subtypes, including metastatic disease, whereas O-RADS provides a structured reporting and management framework. A systematic, evidence-based ultrasound approach improves preoperative risk stratification, facilitates communication among clinicians, optimizes referral to gynecological oncology centers, and helps reduce both unnecessary surgery for benign disease and delayed diagnosis of ovarian cancer.

title: Perioperative management of patients with recent concussion undergoing noncardiac extracranial surgery: A modified Delphi consensus study.
abstract: Many patients present for surgery soon after concussion, when cerebral physiologic regulation may remain disturbed, and no evidence-based guideline or standardized consensus recommendations exist. We sought expert consensus for adults with recent concussion undergoing noncardiac extracranial surgery. We conducted a two-round modified Delphi study (November 2025-March 2026). Round 1 items, drafted from a systematic literature search, included case vignettes. Experts identified by bibliographic screening, directories, and nomination rated items on a five-point Likert scale; "do not know" responses were excluded from the denominator. Consensus was defined a priori as 75% agreement or greater, and strong consensus as 85% or greater. Thirty-five experts (33 anesthesiologists) from 17 countries completed both rounds; 13 of 16 Round 2 statements reached consensus. Agreement was unanimous for preoperative screening for concussion symptoms and neurologic red flags, and for avoidance of hypoxemia, abnormal carbon dioxide tension, sustained hypotension, and marked hypertension. Strong consensus supported generally deferring elective surgery until concussion symptoms resolve (97%), preoperative counseling (97%), structured follow-up (94%), and extended postoperative monitoring in higher-risk patients (91%). Consensus was not reached for regional anesthesia or monitored anesthesia care over general anesthesia (74%), electroencephalography-based depth of anesthesia monitoring (73%), or cautious long-acting neuraxial opioid use (69%). The panel did not define symptom resolution and established no symptom-independent waiting interval or concussion-specific numeric physiologic threshold. This anesthesiology-led consensus supports symptom-guided timing, physiologic stability, counseling, and structured follow-up; anesthetic technique, electroencephalographic monitoring, and neuraxial opioid use remain unresolved. The statements form an expert-informed framework, not an evidence-based practice guideline.

title: Subclinical cardiac autonomic and pulmonary dysfunction in ambulatory patients with cervicothoracic intradural spinal tumours: A prospective cross-sectional study.
journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
abstract: Cervicothoracic intradural spinal tumours (C1-T12) may compromise autonomic and respiratory function due to proximity to sympathetic and cardiopulmonary regulatory centres. This study aimed to evaluate autonomic and pulmonary dysfunction in these patients using heart rate variability (HRV), autonomic function tests (AFTs), pulmonary function tests (PFTs), and echocardiography, with a subgroup analysis comparing intramedullary (IDIM) vs extramedullary (IDEM) conditions. In this prospective cross-sectional study, 68 ambulatory patients (mean age 36.9 ± 12.5 years; 30 male, 38 female) with radiologically confirmed cervicothoracic intradural tumours (Modified McCormick functional grades I-III) and 68 age- and gender-matched healthy, non-smoking controls, free of cardiopulmonary, neurological and endocrine disease and not taking medication, underwent preoperative heart rate variability (HRV) analysis, conventional autonomic function tests (AFT), pulmonary function tests (PFT) and echocardiography. Group comparisons used Student's t or Mann-Whitney U tests. Associations with functional grade were examined using Spearman correlation and chi-square tests. IDIM-IDEM comparisons were unadjusted and exploratory. Compared with controls, patients had lower SDNN (median 26.43 vs 40.01 ms; p = 0.0017), RMSSD (15.13 vs 31.96 ms; p < 0.0001), total power (695.7 vs 1335 ms2), low-frequency (LF) power (178.1 vs 369.1 ms2) and high-frequency (HF) power (106.4 vs 400.5 ms2), higher normalised LF with lower normalised HF, and a higher resting heart rate (84.93 vs 75.19 beats/min; p < 0.0001). Deep-breathing difference, Valsalva ratio, orthostatic heart-rate ratio and handgrip diastolic-pressure response were lower in patients (all p < 0.0001). Forced vital capacity and FEV1 (% predicted), inspiratory capacity, vital capacity, expiratory reserve volume and maximal voluntary ventilation were also lower. None of the HRV, AFT or PFT measures was significantly associated with Modified McCormick functional grade (all p ≥ 0.054). IDIM tumours spanned more vertebral segments than IDEM tumours (more than 3 segments in 56.4 % vs 24.1 %) and the groups differed in age. In unadjusted comparisons, resting heart rate was higher in IDIM tumours, whereas deep-breathing difference, handgrip response, FVC and ERV were lower in IDEM tumours. Ambulatory patients with cervicothoracic intradural spinal tumours demonstrated alterations in cardiac autonomic modulation and pulmonary function despite preserved ambulatory status and the absence of overt cardiopulmonary disease. The cross-sectional design shows associations, not causation. Differences between intramedullary and extramedullary tumours may reflect tumour compartment; they could also reflect differences in tumour level, extent and patient characteristics, and require confirmation in larger studies with adjusted analyses and longitudinal postoperative assessment.

title: IL-17 aggravates the neuroinflammatory response in depression by regulating microglial polarization through the JAK1/STAT3 signaling pathway.
abstract: Background: Microglia-mediated neuroinflammation is closely related to the development of depression. As a proinflammatory cytokine, IL-17 plays a key role in various neuroinflammatory diseases. This study aimed to investigate the potential molecular mechanisms through which IL-17 affects neuroinflammation in depression through the regulation of microglial polarization. Methods: A chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)-induced mouse model of depression and an LPS-treated BV2 cell model were used. The depression-like behavior of the mice was evaluated using the sucrose preference test (SPT), tail suspension test (TST), and forced swim test (FST). Neuronal injury was assessed using HE staining. The levels of neurotransmitters and inflammatory cytokines were analyzed using ELISA. Microglial polarization was analyzed by flow cytometry and immunofluorescence, and the expression of IL-17A and JAK1/STAT3 pathway-related proteins was assessed using Western blotting. Results: IL-17 was highly expressed in clinical specimens from patients with depression, mice treated with CUMS and BV2 cells. The inhibition of IL-17 improved depression-like behavior in CUMS-treated mice, reduced neuronal damage, and increased the expression of the neurotransmitters 5-HT, NE, and DA. In addition, IL-17 inhibition inhibited M1 microglial polarization and inflammation. In terms of molecular mechanisms, IL-17 promoted microglial M1 polarization by activating the JAK1/STAT3 signaling pathway and aggravating neuroinflammation related to depression. The use of the JAK/STAT pathway activator RO8191 attenuated the inhibitory effect of IL-17 inhibition on microglial M1 polarization. Conclusion: IL-17 activates JAK1/STAT3 signaling, promotes M1 microglial polarization, and aggravates neuroinflammation related to depression.

title: Emerging Insights into Autophagy-Lysosomal Dysfunction in Age-Related Neurodegenerative Disorders.
abstract: Ageing is associated with changes in autophagic-lysosomal quality control, but these changes are not uniform and do not necessarily indicate reduced autophagy. This narrative review uses a clearance-bottleneck framework to examine how defects in pathway capacity, cargo recognition, autophagosome formation, trafficking, or lysosomal degradation may affect the ageing nervous system. It integrates evidence on lysosomal function and biogenesis, nutrient-sensing and transcriptional regulation, macroautophagy, chaperone-mediated autophagy, protein turnover, and organelle quality control. The review considers how these processes intersect with protein aggregation, mitochondrial dysfunction, synaptic regulation, and inflammatory communication among neurons, microglia, and astrocytes. Findings across Alzheimer's disease and tauopathies, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis/frontotemporal dementia, and Huntington's disease/polyglutamine disorders are compared with attention to cargo, cellular context, model, and evidence from human studies. Methodological limitations are emphasized, particularly the inability of autophagy markers alone to establish completed flux. Therapeutic studies are evaluated separately for rescue, human target engagement, and clinical benefit. Evidence does not establish that precision correction of a defined neuronal autophagy defect improves clinical outcomes. The framework identifies priorities for validating clearance defects and testing interventions.

title: Mechanisms and Functional Outcomes of Astrocytic Ca2+ Signaling.
abstract: Astrocytic calcium (Ca2+) signaling is a central regulator of brain function, enabling astrocytes to integrate neuronal, vascular, and metabolic information across multiple spatial and temporal scales. Rather than passive support cells, astrocytes generate dynamic Ca2+ signals ranging from localized microdomain transients in perisynaptic processes to propagating intercellular waves. These signals arise from coordinated activity of plasma membrane channels, ligand-gated and G protein-coupled receptors, and intracellular Ca2+ handling systems. Through these mechanisms, astrocytic Ca2+ dynamics regulate essential processes including gliotransmitter release, synaptic modulation and plasticity, neurovascular coupling, and metabolic support. This multiscale signaling framework positions astrocytes as active hubs within the tripartite synapse and neurovascular unit, shaping both local circuit activity and global brain states. Notably, distinct signaling modalities-particularly microdomain events-function as key computational units that enable astrocytes to decode synaptic inputs. Disruption of Ca2+ homeostasis transforms this system into a driver of pathology. Dysregulated signaling promotes astrogliosis, neuroinflammation, excitotoxicity, and impaired neurovascular and metabolic coupling, and is implicated across disorders including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, epilepsy, stroke, and chronic pain. In this review, we highlight key knowledge gaps, including how microdomain and global Ca2+ signals are integrated, how Ca2+ dynamics couple to astrocytic metabolism and gliotransmission, and how these processes are reorganized across physiological and disease states. Addressing these challenges will be essential for deciphering astrocytic signaling logic and identifying precise pharmacological targets.

title: Protocol for isolation of murine neural stem cells from the adult subventricular zone and reprogramming into induced pluripotent stem cells.
abstract: Reprogramming of neural stem cells (NSCs) into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) offers a promising strategy for studying neurological disorders and developing cell-based therapies. Here, we present a protocol for the isolation and expansion of adult subventricular zone (SVZ)-derived NSCs and their reprogramming using a two-factor Oct4/Klf4 strategy. We describe steps for tissue dissection, NSC culture, viral transduction, colony selection, and pluripotency validation. This streamlined approach enables efficient generation of stable iPSC lines while improving safety and reproducibility. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Lázaro-Carot et al.1.

title: Protocol for generating parasympathetic neurons from hiPSCs and their coculture with hiPSC-atrial cardiomyocytes.
abstract: Peripheral parasympathetic ganglia lie adjacent to their target organs and are difficult to access for primary culture; their dysfunction contributes to diseases like atrial fibrillation. Here, we present a protocol to differentiate human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) into parasympathetic neurons and assess their function by electrophysiological recordings, nicotinic receptor activity, and expression of cholinergic and autonomic markers. We also describe how to establish a coculture system with hiPSC-atrial cardiomyocytes that allows neuromodulation of cardiomyocyte activity.

title: DANCE: Step-by-Step Protocol for Automated Quantification of Drosophila Aggression and Courtship.
abstract: Aggression and courtship are widely studied social behaviors in Drosophila melanogaster, but their accurate quantification remains a practical obstacle. Manual scoring of these behaviors is time consuming, prone to inter-observer variability, and difficult to scale, while existing automated tools often require expensive hardware or specialized skills. This article provides step-by-step protocols for implementing DANCE (Drosophila Aggression and Courtship Evaluator), a low-cost platform that combines supervised machine learning classifiers with recording hardware built from repurposed medicine blister packs, acrylic sheets, and consumer smartphones. The protocols describe how to construct the aggression and courtship arenas, acquire standardized videos using a smartphone over a tablet backlight, and process recordings through an automated pipeline that tracks individual flies in FlyTracker and scores behavior using six pretrained JAABA classifiers, one for aggressive lunges and five for the stages of male courtship. Additional protocols describe how to train new classifiers, validate classifier performance against manual annotation, and add an optogenetic stimulation module. Each protocol specifies the required materials, software versions, parameter settings, and expected outputs, so that a user with no prior experience in automated behavioral analysis can generate per-dyad behavioral measurements suitable for statistical comparison. All classifiers, analysis scripts, and worked examples are available at https://github.com/agrawallab/DANCE. The platform was originally described and validated by Yadav et al. (2025). © 2026 The Author(s). Current Protocols published by Wiley Periodicals LLC. Basic Protocol 1: Construction and use of DANCE hardware for recording aggression in Drosophila Support Protocol 1: Preparation of Drosophila for aggression and courtship assays Support Protocol 2: Preparation of aggression food and arena coating Support Protocol 3: Standardized video acquisition for DANCE recordings Basic Protocol 2: Construction and use of DANCE hardware for recording courtship behaviors in Drosophila Basic Protocol 3: Automated quantification of aggression and courtship behaviors Support Protocol 4: Animal tracking using Caltech FlyTracker Support Protocol 5: Score file generation using JAABA classifiers Alternate Protocol 1: Training custom JAABA classifiers Alternate Protocol 2: Ground-truth annotation and classifier validation Alternate Protocol 3: Integration of an optogenetics module.

title: Integrative Genomic and Stem Cell Frameworks for Variant-to-Function Discovery in Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition shaped by de novo protein-truncating variants, inherited missense substitutions, recurrent copy number variations (CNVs), and distributed polygenic risk. These alterations converge on a limited set of neurobiological processes, including synaptic refinement, excitation-to-inhibition balance, chromatin state regulation, and glial-mediated neuroimmune signaling. Experimental paradigms now exist for systematic variant-to-function interrogation through CRISPR-engineered isogenic human pluripotent stem-cell libraries incorporating Cas9 nucleases, programmable transcriptional modulators (dCas9-KRAB and dCas9-VP64), base editors, and prime editing systems. Coupled with single-cell multi-omic platforms such as Perturb-seq, scATAC-seq, and CITE-seq, and with circuit-level phenotyping through multielectrode arrays, calcium imaging, and quantitative morphometry, these systems resolve ASD-relevant cellular states at single-cell and cell-type-specific resolution. In this narrative review, we distinguish deliberately between what these platforms have already established and what remains proposed. To date, a small number of studies constitute the demonstrated evidence base: in vivo Perturb-seq of 35 ASD/neurodevelopmental risk genes in mouse cortex, mosaic knockout of ASD genes in human cortical organoids, the CHOOSE organoid screen of 36 risk genes, assembloid CRISPR screening of 425 neurodevelopmental-disorder risk genes, a 63-line mouse embryonic stem-cell CNV resource, and a CRISPRi screen of 102 ASD risk genes in human induced pluripotent stem-cell (iPSC)-derived microglia implicating ADNP in synaptic pruning. We summarized these in a dedicated comparison table. Against this, integration of polygenic and noncoding architecture, causal-inference frameworks, such as Mendelian randomization and do-calculus, and cross-laboratory reproducibility, remain aspirational rather than realized. We therefore frame the field's principal near-term requirement not as further gene discovery but as harmonized protocols, shared reference lines, arrayed validation capacity, and interpretable statistical frameworks capable of converting perturbation atlases into causal mechanism.

title: Reduced Cytokine Production in a CYFIP1-Mediated Model of Autism Spectrum Disorder.
journal: Bulletin of experimental biology and medicine
abstract: CYFIP1 (Cytoplasmic FMR1 Interacting Protein 1) is a key component of the regulatory complex controlling actin polymerization, which is critically important for neuronal morphogenesis, synapse formation, and the maintenance of synaptic plasticity. Reduced CYFIP1 gene expression is associated with autism spectrum disorder, schizophrenia, epilepsy, and developmental delay. Cyfip1 haploinsufficient (Cyfip1+/-) mice demonstrate not only behavioral deficiency, but also diminished production of cytokines, key regulators of the immune response. This CYFIP1-dependent imbalance of immune system regulators may result in an inadequate response to proinflammatory stimuli in patients with neuropsychiatric symptoms. This phenomenon should be taken into account when developing therapeutic strategies for these patients.

title: Effect of Melatonin in Rectal Suppositories on Neurological Status and Blood S100B Protein Levels in Experimental Acute Brain Ischemia.
journal: Bulletin of experimental biology and medicine
abstract: We studied the effect of melatonin (MT) on the neurological status and serum S100B protein levels in Wistar rats under conditions of experimental acute cerebral ischemia. The animals received daily administrations for 7 days of either a novel 100 mg rectal suppository containing 2.5 mg of MT or a citicoline solution (100 mg/kg, intraperitoneally). On days 3 and 7, neurological status was assessed using the Garcia scale and the limb placing test; serum S100B levels were measured by ELISA. The use of MT-containing suppositories led to a partial recovery of the neurological deficit, improved the limb placing test and Garcia scores, and reduced the serum S100B protein levels. The efficacy of MT in the form of rectal suppositories in correcting neurological deficits was significantly superior to that of the citicoline solution, which may be attributed to optimal pharmacokinetics and pleiotropic mechanisms of action, including direct and indirect antioxidant effects, suppression of neuroinflammation, and modulation of synaptic plasticity. At the same time, citicoline was more efficient in reducing serum S100B protein levels, which is consistent with its primary mechanism of action aimed at repairing cell membranes through enhanced phosphatidylcholine synthesis, leading to stabilization of astrocyte membranes and structural components of the blood-brain barrier.

title: Neurobiology of Treatment-Emergent Mania Associated with Antidepressant: A Narrative Review Update.
abstract: Bipolar disorder (BD) is a complex and debilitating condition in which antidepressant-associated treatment-emergent mania (TEM) poses a significant clinical challenge. This narrative review synthesizes current insights into the neurobiological mechanisms underlying this phenomenon, aiming to update the understanding in the field. Clinical guidelines often caution against antidepressant monotherapy due to the risks of mood destabilization and switching, particularly in BD type I. A review of specific antidepressant classes reveals that tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) carry a high risk of TEM, which has been linked to disruptions in cholinergic-adrenergic balance and heightened noradrenergic activity. Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), while less implicated than TCAs, are also associated with TEM, involving serotonin neurotransmission and potential interactions with muscarinic and histaminergic receptors. Furthermore, evidence suggests that even atypical antidepressants with non-monoaminergic profiles can induce manic switches, highlighting the vulnerability of some individuals and the influence of genetic predispositions. In addition, the effects of antidepressants associated with TEM can also be influenced by factors related to hepatic metabolism, as well as alterations in mitochondrial activity and immunoinflammatory processes, which can modulate the response to treatment and vulnerability to mood dysregulation. Antidepressants are one possible precipitant of TEM, but the phenomenon is better understood as a vulnerability-dependent outcome rather than a universal consequence of antidepressant exposure. Current evidence suggests that TEM may arise from neurobiological perturbations that are partially distinct across antidepressant classes and interact with individual susceptibility factors. These findings point to a broader network-level dysregulation of mood that extends beyond isolated neurotransmitter systems. These observations reinforce the importance of personalized treatment strategies that prioritize mood stabilization, careful patient selection, and close clinical monitoring when antidepressants are used in bipolar depression.

title: Comparison of the neuroprotective effects of tryptamide and ibuprofen in cellular Parkinson's disease models: cell damage type- and cell phenotype-dependent effects.
abstract: Tryptamide (TRP) is an experimental anti-inflammatory and analgesic drug with a favourable safety profile even at high doses. Since neuroinflammation is a significant contributor to the pathogenesis of various neurodegenerative diseases, in this study we screened for the potential direct neuroprotective effect of TRP in comparison to the classical anti-inflammatory compound, ibuprofen (Ibu), in cellular models of Parkinson's disease. We compared the effectiveness of TRP (1-300 µM) with Ibu (10-300 µM) against cell damage induced by oxidative stress inducers (H2O2 and 6-hydroxydopamine, 6-OHDA), dopaminergic neurotoxin 1-methyl-4-phenylpyridinium ion (MPP(+)), and pro-apoptotic factors, staurosporine (St) and doxorubicin (Dox) in undifferentiated (UN-) and retinoic acid (RA)-differentiated human neuroblastoma SH-SY5Y cells. The neuroprotective effects were evidenced by biochemical assays (MTT reduction and LDH release tests), morphology (microscopic evaluation), and caspase-3 activity, as well as validated in mouse primary mesencephalic neurons. We demonstrated that TRP and Ibu at concentrations up to 100 µM, when given for 24 and 48 h, did not evoke any detrimental effects in UN- and RA-SH-SY5Y cells, but induced some cytotoxicity at the highest concentration tested (300 µM) in UN-SH-SY5Y cells. TRP significantly attenuated the cytotoxic effect of MPP(+) in UN- and RA-SH-SY5Y cells and was protective against H2O2, St, and Dox only in differentiated cells, however, it did not attenuate the 6-OHDA-induced cell death in both cell phenotypes. Moreover, the protection of TRP against MPP(+) and St, but not against Dox, was associated with inhibition of caspase-3 activity. Ibu did not show any protection in either of the tested cell models or cell phenotypes, with the exception of minor protection (10 µM) against St in UN-SH-SY5Y cells. The effects of TRP were orthogonally confirmed by high-content imaging of Calcein AM/Hoechst 33,342-stained RA-SH-SY5Y cells exposed to MPP(+) and of tyrosine hydroxylase (TH)-immunostained mouse primary mesencephalic neurons exposed to MPP(+) or 6-OHDA. Our results evidenced a neuroprotective potential of TRP against various cell-damaging factors, with its higher effectiveness in RA-SH-SY5Y cells in apoptotic, rather than oxidative stress-based neuronal cell damage models, which was also confirmed in primary mesencephalic neurons. TRP effects on RA-differentiated neurons were further validated by energy metabolism profile and high-content imaging in the MPP(+) model. Thus, TRP has neuroprotective potential, worth further investigation.

title: Neurobehavioral Assessment of ADHD and Anxiety Co-occurrence in Pediatric Populations.
abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is frequently comorbid with anxiety, a condition that complicates diagnosis and treatment. Stimulant medications used to treat ADHD may exacerbate anxiety in some children, although this is not a consistent effect. This study investigates Alpha Peak Frequency (APF) as a potential neurophysiological marker, alongside Theta/Beta Ratio (TBR) and Sensorimotor Rhythm (SMR), to compare children with ADHD alone (ADHD group) and those with ADHD and comorbid anxiety (COM group) using electrophysiological and behavioral assessments. We assessed 98 children (8-16 years, M = 10.1, SD = 2.25) diagnosed with ADHD based on DSM-5 criteria, divided into ADHD (n = 46) and COM (n = 52) groups. Behavioral measures included the Conners' Parent Rating Scale-Revised (CPRS-R) and the Spence Children's Anxiety Scale (SCAS). EEG data were analyzed to compare APF, TBR, and SMR across frontal, central, and occipital regions. The COM group exhibited significantly higher SCAS anxiety scores but no significant differences in ADHD symptom severity compared to the ADHD group. EEG analysis revealed an overall reduction in APF in the COM group compared to the ADHD group, with multiplicity-adjusted post hoc comparisons confirming significantly lower APF at the central and occipital electrodes. Additionally, compared to the ADHD group, the COM group showed reduced SMR at the central site, lower TBR in the occipital region, and higher occipital beta activity. APF, TBR, and SMR differed between children with ADHD and COM groups. These group differences require replication, and their diagnostic or treatment-related relevance remains to be established.

title: Ultrasound-guided intra-articular steroid injection versus combined suprascapular and axillary nerve block in adhesive capsulitis: a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: To compare ultrasound-guided intra-articular corticosteroid injection with combined suprascapular and axillary nerve block for pain and functional outcomes in primary adhesive capsulitis. In this single-center, assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial, 80 patients were allocated equally to ultrasound-guided intra-articular methylprednisolone (Group A) or combined ultrasound-guided suprascapular and axillary nerve blocks with methylprednisolone and bupivacaine (Group B). Both groups were prescribed home exercises. The primary outcome was baseline-to-week-12 change in visual analog scale (VAS; 0-10) pain scores. Secondary outcomes included the Shoulder Pain and Disability Index (SPADI; 0-100), shoulder range of motion, and quality of life. All 80 patients were included. Mean VAS reductions were 5.27 points in Group A and 5.64 in Group B. The additional Group B reduction was 0.37 points (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.23-0.51; p < 0.001). Mean SPADI reductions were 37.93 and 41.58 points, respectively, with an additional Group B reduction of 3.65 points (95% CI 3.38-3.92; p < 0.001). Both differences were below externally selected, post hoc clinical benchmarks of 1.0 VAS point and 10 SPADI points. Range-of-motion gains varied by movement. Quality-of-life changes could not be established because assessment timing was unverified. No serious adverse events were reported. Both interventions were associated with improvements over 12 weeks. Combined blocks provided small additional reductions in pain and disability, but a clinically important advantage was not demonstrated. IRCT20240901062926N1.

title: Cysteine-related DJ-1 Neuroprotection and AMPK/PGC-1α Responses in Cellular and Mouse Models of Parkinson's Disease.
abstract: Oxidative stress contributes to neuronal injury in Parkinson's disease (PD), and DJ-1 is implicated in cellular antioxidant defense. This study examined the effects of wild-type (WT) DJ-1 and its Cys53 and Cys106 variants in cellular and mouse models of parkinsonism, and assessed the association between DJ-1 and AMPK under oxidizing conditions. SH-SY5Y cells treated with mpp+ and mice treated with MPTP were used to evaluate cell viability, motor behavior, dopaminergic neuron markers, and mitochondrial ultrastructure. Biochemical assays were performed in DJ-1-overexpressing HEK-293FT cells. WT DJ-1 overexpression was associated with improved cell viability and selected behavioral, dopaminergic, and mitochondrial outcomes, whereas the Cys53 and Cys106 variants did not consistently reproduce these effects. Under diamide treatment, DJ-1 and AMPK were detected in a disulfide-linked protein species, and DJ-1 cysteine substitutions altered crosslinking and thiol-labeling signals. Changes in PGC-1α phosphorylation were observed, but AMPK phosphorylation was not significantly altered in the cellular model. Because AMPK and PGC-1α were not functionally manipulated, these findings do not establish that either protein mediates DJ-1-associated effects. The results support protective effects associated with WT DJ-1 overexpression in the models examined and warrant further investigation of the roles of DJ-1 cysteine residues.

title: Correction to: Remote Ischemic Post-Conditioning Modulates Brain Expression of PIWI Proteins After Experimental Cerebral Ischemia.
Longitudinal associations between perceived social support and maternal depression and anxiety across the perinatal period.
abstract: Despite robust international evidence that social support protects maternal mental health, the role of social support across the perinatal period remains poorly understood in Aotearoa New Zealand. This study aimed to examine how perceived social support relates to maternal depression and anxiety during the perinatal period, comparing partner, family, and friend support, and testing whether stress and sleep moderate these associations. Participants were 121 pregnant women who completed monthly surveys over 12 months, including the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, Perinatal Anxiety Screening Scale, and Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support, along with measures of stress and sleep. Linear mixed models tested longitudinal associations and moderation effects. Higher perceived social support was consistently associated with lower depression and anxiety. Family support was the most reliable protective source. Stress predicted higher distress and moderated the effect of support on anxiety, with support being more protective under high stress. Sleep problems predicted greater distress but did not moderate support effects. Findings suggest that perceived social support, particularly from family, is an important protective factor for maternal mental health. Screening for social support and stress in perinatal care may strengthen early identification and guide family-centred interventions.

title: Nicotinic Cholinergic Signaling in Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Secondary Analysis of Receptor Abnormalities and Pharmacological Responses.
abstract: Nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (nAChR) abnormalities and pharmacological responses have been reported in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), but their relationships across human and experimental studies remain unclear. This descriptive secondary analysis used a focused nonsystematic search to select 21 original reports: five human postmortem or molecular, six human pharmacological, and ten experimental ASD-model reports. Comparisons addressed receptor binding, expression and function, percentage differences from published means, exposure-response patterns, antagonist experiments, and compatibility across evidence levels. Human postmortem findings repeatedly showed reduced high-affinity binding and α4/β2-related expression. However, four reports arose from a connected research program, and some binding data were reused. α7 findings varied by region and measurement. Experimental findings differed by model, developmental stage, sex, compound, and outcome. The eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4E (eIF4E) study identified impaired β2-containing receptor function without establishing α4β2 identity. α7-related pharmacological effects and antagonist evidence were outcome-specific; valproate-exposed rats showed both positive and null findings. Nicotine and maternal immune activation experiments provided complementary neuroimmune evidence. Human intervention studies reported preliminary physiological, behavioral, or neurocognitive responses without establishing efficacy. The selected findings support nicotinic pathway involvement, although postmortem dependence and experimental heterogeneity limit generalization. They do not establish a uniform receptor deficit, a shared mechanism across species, or clinical benefit.

title: Identification of Key Fatty acid Metabolism-Related Genes in Vascular Dementia.
abstract: Vascular dementia (VaD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by chronic cerebral hypoperfusion and cognitive decline, yet the role of fatty acid metabolism in its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Integrated transcriptomic profiling was combined with network-based analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and machine learning to uncover key fatty acid metabolism-associated molecular features associated with VaD. Single-cell RNA sequencing, intercellular communication inference, and in silico perturbation analyses were applied to define immune-stromal interactions. Potential therapeutic compounds were evaluated using molecular docking and dynamics simulations. We identified three VaD-related fatty acid metabolism genes (VaD-FAMRGs), namely PNPLA3, HSP90AA1, and ALB, which showed consistent diagnostic performance across multiple computational approaches and were associated with lipid metabolism, inflammatory processes, and neurovascular unit dysfunction. Functional enrichment, single-cell RNA sequencing, and in silico gene perturbation analyses provided exploratory insights into the potential associations of these candidate genes with lipid transport, metabolic regulation, synaptic maintenance, and immune-inflammatory processes. Cell-cell communication analysis further revealed activation of the ANGPTL signaling axis, suggesting impaired endothelial-glial interactions driven by lipid metabolic dysregulation. Regulatory network analysis identified key transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulators, including REST, miR-155-5p, and miR-21-5p, which may coordinately modulate VaD-FAMRG expression. Drug repurposing analysis highlighted quercetin as a candidate compound with predicted interactions with all three hub proteins, supported by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. These findings suggest that dysregulated fatty acid metabolism may be associated with the development and progression of VaD through coordinated metabolic, inflammatory, and neurovascular mechanisms. This study provides a systems-level framework for understanding the underlying pathological processes and establishes a theoretical basis for future mechanistic and experimental validation.

title: Long-term socioeconomic, psychiatric, and societal burden in patients with grade 2 mIDH glioma and partner spillover burden, worsening with disease progression and RT/CT initiation.
abstract: Grade 2 mIDH gliomas affect adults of working age and may disrupt everyday functioning, work capacity, and family life for many years. We assessed long-term socioeconomic, healthcare, and psychiatric burden among patients initially managed with active observation and their partners. This Danish nationwide observational matched cohort study included patients with incident grade 2 mIDH diffuse astrocytoma or oligodendroglioma diagnosed from 2010 to 2022. Patients receiving radiotherapy (RT) and/or chemotherapy (CT), palliative care, or dying within six months after diagnosis were excluded. Patients and partners were compared with coarsened exact matched population controls and outcomes were followed up to 10 years post-index and stratified by RT/CT treatment exposure. The study included 237 patients and 113 partners, matched to 1,161 patient controls and 550 partner controls. Ten-year overall patient survival was 72.7%. Patients experienced a profound and increasing burden: Over 10 years, they averaged - 163,000€ lost pay-check income and accumulated + 347,000€ combined incremental burden from public benefits, healthcare costs, and productivity loss (RT/CT-exposed: +513,000€, RT/CT unexposed: +163,000€) compared to controls. Partners maintained stable income and employment, but partners of RT/CT-exposed patients had increased work absence, averaging + 2.8 excess weeks annually (approximately twice the excess seen among partners of RT/CT-unexposed patients, + 1.4 weeks). Grade 2 IDH-mutant glioma imposes a significant, progressive long term multidimensional burden on patients and society. Disease progression and RT/CT initiation marks a clinically meaningful trajectory shift towards profoundly worse outcomes for patients and partners.

title: Genomic characterization and efficacy of bacteriophages ST22 and ST231 in mitigating Desulfovibrio vulgaris and toxic gases in shrimp aquaculture models.
abstract: This study aims to address the urgent need for antibiotic alternatives in aquaculture by isolating and characterizing novel bacteriophages. The primary objective was to evaluate the efficacy of two newly identified phages, ST22 and ST231, in targeting the sulfate-reducing bacterium Desulfovibrio vulgaris and assessing their potential for environmental remediation and disease management. The researchers utilized Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) to determine morphological features and employed genomic sequencing to analyze the genetic profiles of both phages. Lytic activity was validated through lysis assays, while microcosm experiments were conducted to monitor the reduction of environmental pollutants, specifically H2S and NH3. Finally, in vivo trials with shrimp were performed to confirm biological safety and survival efficacy. Morphological analysis classified ST22 (genus Bruynoghevirus) and ST231 (genus Murrayvirus) as having double-stranded DNA genomes of 45,779 bp and 41,280 bp, respectively. Both phages exhibited potent lytic activity, significantly reducing D. vulgaris density and altering colony morphology. In microcosm settings, phage application effectively mitigated H2S and NH3 levels. Furthermore, a substantial increase in shrimp survival rates underscored their efficacy as safe biocontrol agents. Phages ST22 and ST231 represent promising candidates for sustainable disease management and environmental remediation in aquaculture. These findings validate the potential of phage therapy as a robust, eco-friendly alternative to traditional chemical treatments for bacterial pathogens.

title: Beyond monoamines: a multi-systems molecular framework for major depressive disorder.
abstract: For over five decades, the monoamine hypothesis has anchored the conceptual and pharmacological approach to major depressive disorder (MDD), yet nearly one-third of patients fail to achieve remission with standard antidepressants, and therapeutic response is delayed by weeks. This narrative review offers a critical synthesis of recent high-impact literature drawn on evidence from genomic, molecular, and translational studies across six domains: genomic architecture, epigenetic dysregulation, neuroinflammation, neurotrophic signalling, gut-brain axis, and rapid-acting antidepressant mechanisms, to construct a multi-systems framework of MDD pathophysiology and, as a secondary and explicitly scoped aim, to identify translational priorities for South Asian, particularly Indian, populations; the evidence reviewed is global in scope. A 2025 genome-wide association study (GWAS) of 688,808 cases identified 697 independent associations mapping to 635 genomic risk loci implicating glutamatergic, GABAergic, and neuropeptidergic systems. Environmental stressors converge on this genetic susceptibility through DNA methylation, histone modification, and non-coding RNA-mediated epigenetic reprogramming. An inflammatory MDD subgroup, characterised by kynurenine pathway disruption and microglial dysregulation, is of interest for patient stratification. Rapid-acting antidepressants proposed to act through TrkB-BDNF-dependent synaptic plasticity offer a mechanistic account of their fast onset, although the direct-binding theory awaits independent replication. Gut microbiome dysbiosis, particularly among neurotransmitter-producing taxa, further extends the pathophysiological map beyond the brain itself. Together, these findings support a shift from a unidimensional monoaminergic model to an integrated, multi-systems molecular framework of MDD. Realising the clinical potential of this framework will require validated precision biomarker panels, dedicated South Asian GWAS cohorts, and longitudinal multi-omics studies.

title: Effect of uncertainty in probabilistic reinforcement discrimination tasks.
abstract: Survival in unpredictable environments requires organisms to distinguish between stochastic noise and fundamental shifts in environmental contingencies. Traditional paradigms like the Iowa Gambling Task (IGT) and reversal learning involve multiple confounding variables, such as simultaneous mixed-valence appraisal and history-dependent procedural shifts, that complicate the isolation of specific cognitive processes. To address these limitations, we developed a stationary probabilistic reinforcement discrimination (PRD) task that isolates appetitive (reward) and aversive (relief-based) reinforcement across separate experiments. Using a trial-by-trial analysis within a Bayesian-inspired framework, we modeled how mice navigate uncertainty by weighting stable, long-term prior beliefs against immediate misleading experiences. Our results demonstrate that environmental uncertainty induced by tempering the salience of outcome feedback, promotes a "stickiness" of previously acquired discrimination, anchoring behaviour to established mental models. This effect was consistent across both appetitive and aversive domains, suggesting that while reward and relief are governed by distinct neurobiological substrates, they are processed through similar mental representations during decision-making. Furthermore, we explored physical effort as a non-verbal proxy for decision confidence, finding that performance variability (amplitude variance), rather than effort magnitude per se, serves as a reliable metric for internal confidence. These findings suggest that uncertainty effectively shields prior beliefs from the destabilizing effects of recent information, potentially stunting the prediction errors necessary for new learning. By bridging computational modeling with behavioural flexibility, this study establishes the PRD task as a robust platform for investigating the mechanisms of belief updating in both healthy and pathological states.

title: Tumor-masked structural connectomics for assessing tract-specific white matter disruption associated with glioma aggressiveness: an interpretable machine learning pilot study.
abstract: To assess the feasibility of personalized tumor-masked structural connectomics combined with interpretable machine learning (ML) for differentiating low-grade gliomas (LGG) from high-grade gliomas (HGG), and to identify candidate tract-specific connectomic biomarkers of glioma aggressiveness. Thirty-five patients with histopathologically confirmed gliomas (20 LGG, 15 HGG) underwent preoperative diffusion tensor imaging and T1-weighted MRI. Tumor-masked probabilistic tractography was used to reconstruct individualized structural connectomes based on 50 white matter (WM) tract labels. We evaluated 296 graph-theoretical features using sequential feature selection and Random Forest classification within a strictly isolated nested cross-validation framework. We used SHAP analysis for model interpretation. Sensitivity analyses compared clinical-radiological, connectomic, and combined feature sets. The leak-free pure connectomics model achieved a mean ROC-AUC of 0.814 ± 0.327 (95% CI, 0.500-1.000), with a macro-F1 score of 0.786 ± 0.265. Restricting the analysis to non-zero connectomic features yielded a mean AUC of 0.833 ± 0.167. The clinical-radiological model achieved a mean AUC of 0.817 ± 0.149, while the combined clinical-radiological and connectomic model showed the highest point estimate (AUC, 0.933 ± 0.109; 95% CI, 0.798-1.068). SHAP analysis highlighted the sagittal stratum, medial lemniscus, and superior fronto-occipital fasciculus among the most informative WM pathways. Tumor-masked structural connectomics combined with interpretable ML demonstrated preliminary feasibility for identifying candidate imaging biomarkers associated with glioma aggressiveness in neuroradiological practice. These findings are exploratory and represent internal estimates from a single cohort; external validation in independent, multi-center cohorts is required before any potential clinical application.

title: Neuropharmacology of omega-3 long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids in neurodegenerative diseases: mechanisms, multi-omics evidence, and clinical translation.
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, involve progressive neuronal dysfunction associated with neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial impairment, defective proteostasis, and synaptic failure. Although symptomatic treatment remains central, anti-amyloid therapies can modestly slow clinical decline in selected patients with early Alzheimer's disease. This review critically evaluates the neuropharmacological evidence for omega-3 long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids, particularly docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) and eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), and the barriers to their clinical translation. We narratively synthesized preclinical, observational, and interventional clinical evidence, focusing on membrane organization, inflammatory resolution, mitochondrial and redox homeostasis, autophagy, proteostasis, neuronal signaling, and factors contributing to heterogeneous clinical outcomes. Preclinical studies support context-dependent effects of DHA and EPA on neuronal membranes, inflammatory signaling, mitochondrial function, redox balance, autophagy, and synaptic plasticity. Human evidence is less consistent: observational studies generally report favorable associations between omega-3 status and neurological outcomes, whereas randomized trials show null, modest, or subgroup-dependent effects. Outcomes vary with disease stage, baseline omega-3 status, formulation, dose, treatment duration, genotype, and endpoint selection. Uncertain central nervous system exposure and limited pharmacokinetic and target-engagement data remain major translational barriers. Omega-3 long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids are biologically plausible neuropharmacological modulators, but current evidence does not establish DHA or EPA as broadly effective disease-modifying treatments for neurodegenerative diseases. Future trials should prioritize early-stage, biomarker-stratified populations, pharmacologically characterized formulations, adequate treatment duration, and clinically meaningful progression-related outcomes.

title: Design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel p-tert-Butylcalix[4]arene derivatives bearing maleimide units as potential anticancer agents.
journal: Medicinal chemistry research : an international journal for rapid communications on design and mechanisms of action of biologically active agents
abstract: In this study, a novel series of seven p-tert-butylcalix[4]arene derivatives functionalized with lower-rim aminomaleimide moieties (4a-g) was designed, synthesized, and evaluated for its in vitro antiproliferative potential. Initial biological screening against the U87-MG glioblastoma and normal L929 fibroblast cell lines identified the ethyl-substituted derivative (4b) and the benzyl-substituted derivative (4c) as early-stage screening hits with moderate activity, exhibiting IC50 values of 55.94 ± 4.87 µM and 59.47 ± 7.60 µM, respectively. Compound 4b was selected for further evaluation due to its relatively more favorable selectivity profile (Selectivity Index = 3.72) against normal fibroblasts compared to 4c. Leveraging the intrinsic photophysical properties of the synthesized scaffold, the cellular internalization of 4b in U87-MG cells was visualized via confocal microscopy without the need for external fluorescent tagging. Subsequent in vitro evaluations provided preliminary flow cytometric evidence of dose-dependent apoptosis-associated cell death, showed an inhibition of clonogenic survival (reducing colony formation to 1.1%), and demonstrated the suppression of 3D tumor spheroid formation and growth. Consequently, the calix [4]arene-aminomaleimide framework is established not as a direct systemic anti-glioblastoma agent, but as a preliminary supramolecular screening hit. Its future development strictly requires significant structural optimization to improve its general physicochemical profile and efficacy, alongside the implementation of advanced localized delivery systems to overcome blood-brain barrier restrictions. Compound 4b is shown with reported half-maximal inhibitory concentrations of 55.94 plus or minus 4.87 micromolar for U87-MG glioblastoma cells and 208.19 plus or minus 12.75 micromolar for normal L929 cells. The stated mechanism is apoptosis induction and three-dimensional spheroid disruption. Microscopy images show fluorescence in U87-MG cells but little in L929 cells.

title: Exposure to violence in public places in the country of resettlement and its associations with psychosocial well-being and mental health among children and young adults with refugee backgrounds: a systematic review.
abstract: Children and young adults with refugee backgrounds face various forms of adversity during migration. To facilitate synthesis of this literature, violence in public places (ViPP) was conceptualised as an analytical umbrella framework encompassing different forms of intentional violence occurring in public or community settings, including direct victimisation, witnessing violence, or hearing about violence experienced by others. This review synthesises evidence on the prevalence and forms of such exposure and its associations with psychosocial well-being and mental health among children and young adults with refugee backgrounds. Eight databases (ERIC, PubMed, PsycINFO, Scopus, Web of Science, EconLit, Google Scholar and CINAHL) and 16 grey literature sources were systematically searched for quantitative studies published up to May 2025.
