Eligible studies included participants with refugee backgrounds, had a mean study population age of ≤ 24 years, reported quantitative data on violence exposure in public or community settings corresponding to the ViPP framework, and assessed psychosocial well-being and/or mental health outcomes. Quality appraisal was performed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tool and findings were synthesised narratively. Seven studies were included from 15,109 screened articles, comprising 759 participants with refugee backgrounds who were forcibly displaced from six geographical regions. All included studies examined violence exposures in countries of resettlement among refugee populations who had experienced cross-border displacement. Violence exposures corresponding to the ViPP framework were common, particularly indirect victimisation and witnessing violence, with prevalence ranging from 19% to 66%. Higher levels of violence exposure were associated with poorer psychosocial and mental health outcomes, although findings were heterogeneous, and evidence on specific forms of violence and subgroup differences was limited. The findings indicate that violence exposure may continue after resettlement and highlight violence exposure in public and community settings as an under-recognised post-migration risk. The ViPP framework may facilitate a broader understanding of violence occurring in public and community settings among refugee populations after resettlement.

title: Associations between white matter network alterations and visuospatial and social-emotional deficits in patients with right hemisphere tumors: a prospective clinico-radiological study.
abstract: Preserving neurological function is crucial in brain tumor surgery. Because the right hemisphere supports visuospatial and social‑cognitive abilities, damage may affect quality of life. This prospective study (TANGO; ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04288505) examined associations between visuospatial and social‑emotional deficits and tractography‑based white matter alterations in patients with right hemisphere tumors. Thirty‑four patients were assessed preoperatively and 22 postoperatively using diffusion magnetic resonance imaging and four neuropsychological tests. Tractography metrics were extracted for nine right hemisphere tracts. Thirty‑four Human Connectome Project participants served as controls. Preoperatively, deficits in visuospatial functioning, facial emotion recognition, and mentalizing were associated with predominantly right hemisphere microstructural abnormalities within distributed white matter networks. Visuospatial deficits were associated with alterations involving the frontal aslant tract (FAT), arcuate fasciculus (AF), superior longitudinal fasciculus (SLF), and SLF II; facial emotion recognition deficits with the SLF III and uncinate fasciculus (UF); and mentalizing deficits with the AF. Postoperatively, exploratory findings suggested associations between new social-emotional deficits and structural alterations involving the inferior longitudinal fasciculus (ILF), SLF, and SLF III, whereas new visuospatial deficits showed a trend toward reduced right FAT volume. Relative to controls, left hemisphere tractographic changes were observed regardless of the presence of visuospatial and/or social-emotional deficits, whereas right hemisphere alterations were primarily observed in patients with such deficits. These findings highlight the role of right hemisphere networks in supporting visuospatial and social-emotional functioning. Further characterization of white matter connectivity may help improve risk stratification, surgical planning, and rehabilitation strategies.

title: Endovascular treatment for cervical internal carotid artery occlusion due to dissection: a multicenter analysis.
abstract: Evidence on endovascular treatment (EVT) for isolated cervical internal carotid artery occlusion (c-ICA-O) due to dissection is limited. We evaluated the impact of EVT for dissection-related isolated (non-tandem) c-ICA-O. This secondary analysis of the multicenter EVT for Isolated cervical Internal Carotid Artery occlusion (ETIICA) retrospective study included patients with dissections. Patients treated with EVT were compared with those treated with best medical treatment alone. The primary endpoint was 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) shift analysis. Secondary outcomes included mRS 0-2 or return to baseline, early neurological deterioration (END), symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH), carotid patency at the end of EVT, and intracranial embolization. Analyses used regressions with inverse probability of treatment weighting. Of 998 patients, 108 (10.8%) had dissection [mean age 53.7 (SD 11.2) years, 26.9% female]. EVT was performed in 60 (55.5%) patients. EVT patients had higher admission NIHSS (median 13 [4-18] vs 2 [0-9]). There was no difference in mRS shift (acOR 0.80, 95% CI: 0.29-2.20). Functional independence was observed in 64.9% of EVT patients vs 81.3% of BMT patients (aOR 1.69, 95% CI: 0.52-5.51; BMT as reference). END was numerically more frequent in the EVT group (28.8% vs 8.3%; aOR 2.38, 95% CI: 0.62-9.18). sICH occurred in 2 EVT patients. Carotid patency was achieved in 45/60 (75%) patients undergoing EVT, and 18/59 (30%) patients had intracranial embolization. In this exploratory analysis, EVT was not associated with improved 3-month functional outcomes, despite achieving carotid patency in three out of four patients. Question What are the technical and clinical outcomes of EVT compared with best medical treatment in patients with isolated cervical internal carotid artery occlusive dissection? Findings EVT effectively recanalized acutely occluded dissected extracranial internal carotid arteries, but intracranial emboli and re-occlusion were frequent, with no adjusted 90-day clinical benefit. Clinical relevance Precaution and technical refinement of EVT for isolated cervical carotid artery dissection appear necessary. Larger studies focusing on severely affected patients are warranted. Until such evidence is available, treatment decisions should be individualized on a case-by-case basis.

title: T1 contrast at the gray-white matter boundary during adolescence and its associations with cortical thickness and gyrification.
abstract: The advent of surface-based morphometry has facilitated the detailed evaluation of cortical features such as thickness and folding. However, developmental and clinical studies yield inconsistent findings across these cortical indices, partly due to biological and methodological factors that contribute to their estimation. Using T1-weighted images from over 500 healthy participants in the Philadelphia Neurodevelopmental Cohort (PNC), we investigated age-related differences in T1 contrast at the gray-white matter boundary (T1 contrast) during adolescence and assessed its impact on the estimation of the age-related differences of cortical thickness and local gyrification index. T1 contrast showed a significant positive correlation with age. With increasing age, cortical thickness exhibited a linear decline, whereas local gyrification index exhibited a quadratic decline. Controlling for T1 contrast attenuated the associations between age and both cortical indices. Furthermore, white matter volume was significantly associated not only with T1 contrast but also with cortical thickness and local gyrification index. Nevertheless, age-related associations of both cortical indices remained significant after accounting for T1 contrast. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for T1 contrast when interpreting age-related differences in cortical measures in developmental neuroimaging research.

title: Brain renin-angiotensin system: Pathophysiological mechanisms and therapeutic targets in ischemic stroke.
abstract: This review aims to delineate the context-dependent, opposing actions of the angiotensin II type 1 receptor, angiotensin II type 2 receptor, and angiotensin-converting enzyme 2/ angiotensin-(1-7)/Mas receptor axis in ischemic stroke and to discuss their translational potential for neuroprotective therapy. Although recanalization cannot guarantee favorable functional outcomes for all patients with ischemic stroke, adjunctive neuroprotective targets remain limited. Dysregulation of the brain renin-angiotensin system is increasingly recognized as a potentially modifiable pathway in post-stroke brain injury. Cerebral ischemia shifts the physiological receptor balance toward angiotensin II type 1 receptor predominance, promoting vasoconstriction, blood-brain barrier disruption, neuroinflammation, excitotoxicity, mitochondrial dysfunction, and apoptosis. Conversely, the angiotensin II type 2 receptor and Mas receptor may counter these detrimental processes through temporally distinct mechanisms. The angiotensin II type 2 receptor may provide early neuroprotection through endothelial nitric oxide synthase-mediated vasodilation, suppression of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate oxidase, and inhibition of nuclear factor kappa-B signaling. By comparison, Mas receptor activation may facilitate delayed brain repair through mitochondrial stabilization, nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2-mediated antioxidant responses, and preservation of blood-brain barrier integrity. This temporal framework, characterized by acute injury associated with angiotensin II type 1 receptor signaling, early protection associated with angiotensin II type 2 receptor signaling, and long-term recovery potentially supported by Mas receptor signaling, provides a rationale for time-sensitive therapeutic strategies. Preclinical evidence supports the neuroprotective effects of angiotensin II type 1 receptor blockers. Angiotensin II type 2 receptor agonists, such as compound 21, and glycosylated angiotensin-(1-7) peptide derivatives are promising approaches for engaging endogenous protective pathways.

title: MM102 promotes axonal regeneration and synaptic remodeling through membrane lipid remodeling to restore motor function after spinal cord injury.
abstract: Spinal cord injury causes neurological deficits and dysfunction, but effective pharmacological strategies that promote neural regeneration and functional recovery are lacking. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic potential of MM102, a small-molecule inhibitor of the MLL1-WDR5 interaction, for injured spinal cord repair. HT22 cells were treated with 10 nM MM102 for 6 days, followed by phenotypic evaluation and integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses. MM102 significantly promoted neurite outgrowth and synaptogenesis and increased the expression of the neuronal markers Nestin, synaptophysin, microtubule-associated protein-2, and βIII-tubulin. In vivo, rats with spinal cord injury received MM102 treatment (50 μM, 10 μL/100 g) for 5 weeks, and MM102 repaired spinal cord histoarchitecture, promoted axonal and myelin regeneration and synaptic remodeling, and enhanced locomotor and electrophysiological recovery. Histological staining revealed enhanced axonal and myelin regeneration following MM102 treatment, whereas immunofluorescence analysis revealed significantly increased expression of Nestin, NeuN, c-Jun, NF-200, MBP, and βIII-tubulin. Transcriptomic analysis indicated that MM102 induced gene expression programs associated with neuronal development, axon guidance and synaptic plasticity, whereas metabolomic profiling revealed prominent changes in membrane lipid abundance and neuroactive metabolism. Integrated multiomics analysis further associated these transcriptional responses with membrane phospholipid remodeling and pathways involved in neurotransmitter signaling and synaptic vesicle cycling. Collectively, these findings suggest that MM102 facilitates injured spinal cord repair by modulating responses associated with neural repair and membrane lipid remodeling, also provide novel insights into the potential mechanisms through which small-molecule inhibitors can promote neurogenic potential and elucidate potential therapeutic targets for facilitating functional recovery following spinal cord injury.

title: Globus Pallidus Externus α-Band Activity Decreases After Deep Brain Stimulation in Clinically Responsive Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder Patients.
journal: Neuromodulation : journal of the International Neuromodulation Society
abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) of the anterior limb of the internal capsule (ALIC) is an effective treatment for severe obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). Identifying brain readouts of a positive response may guide further DBS optimization. We measured local field potential (LFP) changes from bilateral DBS leads in ten patients with OCD who were implanted at a uniform tractographic network target derived from prior DBS responders. We consistently stimulated dorsal lead contacts in the ALIC white matter while recording LFP from the ventral lead contacts in the grey matter of the anterior globus pallidus externus (GPe), a key node in the basal ganglia nonmotor indirect pathway. After six months of DBS, OCD symptoms decreased by 40% on average across patients, along with a significant decrease in α-activity across both hemispheres. Only one patient did not have an improvement in symptoms, and this was also the only patient who never exhibited a decrease in α in either hemisphere. Our findings suggest that therapeutic ALIC DBS coincides with a stable decrease in limbic-cognitive GPe α-power, which should be further investigated as a potential biomarker of sustained response.

title: [Pharmacological treatment options for adult attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder].
journal: Psychiatria Hungarica : A Magyar Pszichiatriai Tarsasag tudomanyos folyoirata
abstract: Adult attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a relatively common and largely underdiagnosed neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by symptoms of inattention, impulsivity, impaired activity regulation, and emotional dysregulation, which may cause functional impairment throughout the lifespan. In Hungary, the condition is estimated to affect approximately 250 000 adults, and in many cases it does not lead to help-seeking until young adulthood. Its clinical significance extends well beyond attentional difficulties: ADHD is frequently associated with substance use disorders, mood and anxiety disorders, and, in the longer term, an increased risk of cardiovascular and metabolic conditions. Recognition and appropriate treatment of ADHD therefore offer not only an opportunity for symptom reduction and improved functioning, but also for the prevention of psychiatric and substance use-related complications. The cornerstone of treatment is a multimodal approach: pharmacotherapy is complemented by psychoeducation, structured interventions targeting everyday functioning, and psychotherapy when indicated. In this review, we provide an overview of the currently available pharmacological treatment options for adult ADHD, including the assessments required before treatment initiation, stimulant and non-stimulant medications, and other pharmacological options. We also discuss the benefits, challenges, and clinical significance of long-term pharmacological management. Keywords: attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder; ADHD; pharmacological treatment; stimulant; methylphenidate; lisdexamfetamine; atomoxetine; antidepressant.

title: Brain-penetrating and lesion-triggered hydrogen sulfide nanocarrier for multiple pathogenic interventions in Parkinson's disease therapy.
abstract: The defective hydrogen sulfide (H2S) metabolism in brain has emerged as a crucial pathogenic event and therapeutic target in Parkinson's disease (PD). However, current H2S delivery approaches for PD remain predominantly limited by the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and on-demand supply. This work aimed to upgrade the delivery of H2S to across BBB, thereby adequately harnessing its neuroprotective effect in PD brain. We developed a brain-penetrating, ROS-responsive H₂S nanocarrier (RVG29/TK@Lip/GYY) for targeted H₂S delivery in the PD brain. In this system, the H₂S donor GYY4137 was encapsulated within the liposomal core, and a ROS-responsive thioketal (TK) linker was incorporated into the lipid bilayer to enable on-demand H₂S release in the oxidative PD microenvironment. The liposomal surface was modified with the brain-homing peptide RVG29 to facilitate BBB crossing and neuronal targeting. This formulation achieved a good BBB penetration rate of 22.12%. In addition, pathological evaluation demonstrated that the controlled H2S release by RVG29/TK@Lip/GYY exerted multiple PD pathogenic interventions, including scavenging excessive ROS, alleviating nitrative stress, decreasing neuronal apoptosis, suppressing glial cell activation, and promoting nerve regeneration. Importantly, RVG29/TK@Lip/GYY treatment significantly attenuated the motor deficits of PD model mice. Collectively, this study not only provides a promising H2S nanocarrier for PD multiple pathological therapy, but also contributes to the development of H2S delivery in other neurodegenerative diseases treatment.

title: Retinal neuroprotection and microglia M1/M2 polarization modulation of triamcinolone acetonide and basic fibroblast growth factor co-delivered in liposomes after optic nerve injury.
abstract: Optic nerve diseases can result in the degeneration of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and their axons, ultimately causing irreversible blindness. Current conventional treatments are limited by inconsistent efficacy, adverse effects or poor tolerability, underscoring the urgent need for more effective therapeutic approaches. Triamcinolone acetonide (TA) and basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF) have been identified as neuroprotective agents; however, investigations into their combined effects remain scarce. The present study describes a PEG-modified liposome co-encapsulating TA and bFGF, administered via intravitreal injection in a murine model of optic nerve crush (ONC). This co-delivery system demonstrates superior effects in protecting RGCs, promoting axonal regeneration, and modulating microglia M1/M2 shift compared to the monotherapies. RNA sequencing analysis and molecular experiments revealed that TA/bFGF@Lipo was involved in the NF-κB/p65 signaling pathway and PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. Notably, the expression of tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases-1 (TIMP1) was significantly upregulated following the liposomes treatment and exhibited a strong correlation with the expression of microglia M2 biomarkers. Subsequent experiments demonstrated that rmTIMP1 promoted BV2 microglia M1/M2 shift in a dose-dependent manner, and TIMP1 knockdown significantly decreased the RGCs survival and M2 polarization of retinal microglia induced by TA/bFGF@Lipo. Collectively, this research establishes TA/bFGF@Lipo as an effective therapeutic strategy for optic nerve injury, and highlights the essential role of TIMP1 in RGCs protection and microglia M2 polarization, offering novel insights for the treatment of optic nerve diseases.

title: Smoking and dementia risk: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of 61 prospective cohort studies and implications for tobacco control.
abstract: Smoking has been identified as a modifiable dementia risk factor by three Lancet Commissions, yet dementia remains absent from most tobacco control strategies. The magnitude of the association across dementia subtypes, smoking categories, and population characteristics has not been comprehensively synthesised since 2015. PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, and PsycINFO were searched from January 2013 to 31 August 2026, updating the 2015 review, which contributed 34 studies. Random-effects meta-analyses (Restricted Maximum Likelihood (REML) with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment) estimated pooled relative risks (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Subgroup analyses with tests for interaction and meta-regression examined effect modification by baseline age, ethnicity, follow-up duration, and adjustment for sex, education and Apolipoprotein E ε4 (APOE ε4) genotype. Risk of bias was assessed using Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Exposures (ROBINS-E). Heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran's Q, I2 and τ2 and publication bias using funnel plots and Egger's test. Dose-response analysis of smoking and dementia risk was performed. Smoking population attributable fractions (PAF, unweighted and communality-weighted) for the risk of dementia were calculated. This study is registered with PROSPERO, CRD42025644539. Sixty-one cohort studies (approximately 2.8 million participants) were included. Current smoking was associated with increased risk of all-cause dementia (RR 1.31 [95% CI 1.23-1.39]; number of studies (k) = 39), Alzheimer's disease (1.40 [1.08-1.80]; k = 15), and vascular dementia (1.52 [1.20-1.93]; k = 9). Former smoking was not associated with any outcome, and former smokers had a lower risk of all-cause dementia than current smokers (RR 0.81 [0.75-0.88]). I2 ranged from 0% to 80%. Egger's test suggested small-study effects only for current smoking and all-cause dementia (P = 0.09). The communality-weighted PAF for smoking and dementia was 2.2% (95% CI 1.7-2.8). Dementia risk increased with smoking intensity as the pooled RR was 1.16 (95% CI 1.09-1.23) at 10 cigarettes per day and rose to 1.34 (95% CI 1.18-1.51) at 20 cigarettes per day. Current smoking is consistently associated with higher risk of all dementia outcomes and increases with smoking intensity. Estimates refer to clinically diagnosed dementia syndromes [Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders/International Classification of Diseases (DSM/ICD)] and not to biologically defined disease. Although causality cannot be established from observational data, these findings support considering dementia and brain health outcomes in national tobacco control strategies and associated campaigns. Future work using objectively verified smoking histories is needed to clarify how age at cessation and time since quitting influence dementia risk and whether these effects interact with total years of active smoking. None.

title: The Scandinavian Neurotrauma Committee 2026 guidelines for initial management of minimal, mild and moderate head injuries in adults: a systematic review, meta-analysis and modified Delphi consensus study.
abstract: Several clinical guidelines exist to identify intracranial injury (ICI) after head injury. The Scandinavian Neurotrauma Committee (SNC) published evidence- and consensus-based guidelines in 2000, updated in 2013. Since then, demographic changes, including an ageing population and increased use of antithrombotic therapy have prompted further revision. The aim of this study is to provide a clinically relevant update to the SNC guidelines for the initial management of adults with minimal, mild, or moderate head injury. A PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis addressed population, exposure, comparator, and outcome questions on which emergency department patients with minimal or mild head injury require head computed tomography (CT), direct discharge, in-hospital observation, or repeat CT. Evidence was graded using the GRADE approach. Recommendations were developed through a modified Delphi process with stakeholder review. Twenty-nine stakeholders participated in developing a seven-point recommendation set and updated management flowcharts. Key changes include reduced emphasis on routine CT in patients receiving direct oral anticoagulants, incorporation of glial fibrillary acidic protein and ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1 biomarkers, and use of structured observation as an alternative to CT in selected risk groups. The updated guidelines support risk-adapted imaging and observation strategies that may reduce unnecessary CT scans and hospital admissions, although further validation of safety and effectiveness is needed. No specific funding.

title: Cross-cultural adaptation and psychometric evaluation of the long-form mini nutritional assessment (MNA-LF) among older Moroccan patients with cancer.
abstract: Malnutrition is common among older adults with cancer and independently predicts treatment-related toxicity, functional decline, and mortality. Despite the widespread international use of the Mini Nutritional Assessment Long Form (MNA-LF), no Moroccan Arabic version had previously been available. To adapt the MNA-LF into Moroccan Arabic and evaluate its reliability, exploratory component structure, convergent validity, and concurrent discriminative validity against selected anthropometric and functional muscle-related criteria among older Moroccan patients with cancer. A cross-sectional psychometric evaluation study was conducted following a five-stage cross-cultural adaptation process. Three public Moroccan hospital centers. A total of 387 patients aged ≥60 years with histologically confirmed cancer were included. Test-retest reliability was assessed in a subsample of 19 participants. Internal consistency, test-retest reliability, exploratory principal component analysis, convergent validity, and concurrent discriminative validity against selected muscle-related criteria were evaluated. Principal component analysis identified an exploratory six-component solution explaining 60.5% of the total variance. Internal consistency was acceptable (Cronbach's alpha = 0.757; McDonald's omega = 0.776; bootstrap 95% CI, 0.734-0.804), and test-retest reliability was excellent in a small subsample (ICC = 0.928; 95% CI, 0.825-0.971; n = 19). Convergent validity was supported by significant correlations with calf circumference (rho = 0.566) and body mass index (rho = 0.501), although these measures overlap with MNA-LF content. Concurrent discriminative validity against the low-MAMC and low-handgrip-strength criteria was acceptable (AUC = 0.767 and 0.702, respectively); at the ≤17 threshold, specificity exceeded sensitivity for both criteria (82.4%vs. 57.3% and 90.6% vs. 40.4%, respectively). The Moroccan Arabic MNA-LF showed acceptable internal consistency, excellent short-term test-retest reliability in a small subsample (n = 19), and evidence of convergent validity and concurrent discriminative validity against selected muscle-related criteria. Its exploratory component structure requires confirmation in an independent sample. The instrument may support initial nutritional assessment in geriatric oncology and prompt more comprehensive evaluation in accordance with local practice; it is not a diagnostic tool for malnutrition or sarcopenia.

title: A review on the beneficial and detrimental roles of gut microbiota-derived trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMAO).
abstract: In recent years, increasing attention has focused on the role of the gut microbiome in converting dietary substances into bioactive metabolites implicated in the etiology of various diseases. Among these metabolites, trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMAO), a gut microbial metabolite derived from choline, carnitine, and betaine, has emerged as a novel molecule of interest as an alternative messenger with multiple, tissue-specific effects on human physiology. Once considered a benign osmolyte in marine organisms, TMAO is now implicated in human health risks through mechanisms involving oxidative stress, inflammation, and metabolic regulation. While elevated TMAO levels are associated with cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and neurodegeneration, evidence also highlights its cytoprotective properties, including protein stabilization and osmoprotection. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of TMAO's dual role in oxidative stress, inflammation, and endothelial mechanisms, clarifying its context-dependent effects and therapeutic implications.

title: Toward effective therapies for tRNA synthetase-associated diseases.
Disarming oxidized lipids: AAV-delivered antibody neutralization as an emerging strategy against ALS.
The RNA and protein landscapes of mouse brain organoids.
abstract: Organoids are powerful models of brain development and function. Mouse brain organoids reproduce the main steps of neurodevelopment in vivo and differentiate more rapidly than human organoids, making them scalable for screening applications. However, mouse brain organoids remain poorly defined. Here, we showed that the transcriptome and proteome of mouse brain organoids developed for three weeks are close to those of a neonatal mouse brain. Strikingly, organoids recapitulated the majority of alternative splicing and polyadenylation-site events that define neural identity in vivo. Proteomics revealed that most changes in mRNA expression were translated into proteins. Mouse brain organoids differentiated for only three weeks already harbored a complex network of synaptic proteins, including the ionotropic and metabotropic receptors for the neurotransmitters glutamate and GABA. To conclude, our study provides evidence that mouse brain organoids are a rapidly maturing and relevant model of mammalian brain development and function in a neonatal-like environment.

title: A benchmarking framework for organoid computing.
abstract: Organoid computing leverages functional neural networks of lab-grown neural organoids to recapitulate key aspects of human brain information processing, holding promising potential in brain-inspired computing, brain-computer interfaces, neuroscience, and medicine. However, its broad application remains constrained due to technical limitations including biological variability, interface instability, stochastic performance, and limited reproducibility. Here, we present a benchmarking framework that systematically quantifies the key performance determinants of organoid computing. We operationally define 'benchmark-ready' organoid substrates using optional criteria encompassing viability, cellular identity, structural integrity, functional maturation, and baseline networks, supported by multimodal phenotyping. We further establish qualification metrics for organoid-machine interface and intrinsic neural and network function, including physical coupling, spatial coverage, temporal stability, spontaneous activity, and network-level organization. Finally, we introduce a hierarchical evaluation framework for stimulation-evoked computation combined with information encoding criteria, standardized scoring, and statistical reporting. We believe that the benchmarking framework may provide an adaptable foundation for standardized, reproducible and comparable evaluation of organoid computing technologies, thereby facilitating the broad adoption and application of organoid intelligence.

title: Characterization of lysine methylation during neuronal differentiation of LUHMES cells.
abstract: Over one-third of human lysine methyltransferases (KMTs) and lysine demethylases (KDMs) are linked to neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). Changes in histone lysine methylation during neuronal differentiation have been reported. It is now recognized that KMTs and KDMs also target non-histone proteins, yet characterization of non-histone lysine methylation during neuronal differentiation remains limited. Here, we address this gap using quantitative mass spectrometry-based proteomics to quantify changes in non-histone lysine methylation across three stages of the Lund human mesencephalic (LUHMES) neuronal differentiation model. We identify 70 lysine methylation events with significant differences in abundance across differentiation. Our analysis reveals lysine methylation on many non-histone proteins involved in neuronal differentiation, including signaling molecules, cytoskeletal proteins, RNA splicing factors, and transcription factors. This work broadens the understanding of non-histone lysine methylation in a neuronal differentiation model and provides a resource of lysine methylation sites on proteins of biological and clinical significance for future research.

title: Optimized GENE TARGET framework characterizes barriers to therapeutic development for monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders.
abstract: GENE TARGET is a previously published framework designed to quantitatively assess the suitability of a specific monogenic neurodevelopment disorder (NDD) for development of genetic therapies, addressing the need for a systematic and rigorous approach to research prioritization and resource allocation. Here, to keep pace with the rapidly evolving knowledgebase, we refined the framework with more nuanced scoring definitions and added a resource guide to standardize evaluation of each criterion. Interrater agreement was assessed and found to be substantial for most domain/criteria scores among experienced users, primarily genetic counselors with at least two years of experience in translational genomic medicine. Secondary scoring adjudication by experts with clinical/molecular genetics and preclinical modeling expertise is recommended. Cross-disorder analysis of 57 NDD gene-disorder pairs evaluated at the Translational Neuroscience Center was performed, which identified clinical considerations, including establishing endpoints, as the most common translational research gap. Common barriers across disorders also included generating natural history data, establishing an early diagnosis, understanding dosage sensitivity, and demonstrating phenotypic reversibility. We further discuss application of this framework for gene editing and small molecules approaches. Future goals include the validation of GENE TARGET beyond academic research settings and the use of artificial intelligence to aid in preliminary scoring.

title: The Immune-Nanomedicine Axis in Glioblastoma: From Biomimetic Delivery to Immune Reprogramming.
abstract: The therapeutic efficacy against glioblastoma (GBM) remains strictly limited by the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and the profoundly immunosuppressive network of the tumor microenvironment. To overcome these barriers, nanomedicine has shifted from conventional cytotoxin delivery toward the active functional reprogramming of the GBM immune microenvironment. Unlike existing literature that predominantly catalogues nanomaterial properties, this review maps the emerging immune-nanomedicine axis, focusing on recent preclinical proof-of-concept studies to decode how engineered platforms actively reprogram specific cellular compartments within this pathological niche. We evaluate nanoplatforms that utilize biomimetic camouflage and cellular hitchhiking to bypass the BBB and repolarize the myeloid stroma, as well as macroscopic implantable scaffolds designed to immunologically remodel the postoperative resection cavity. To link these innate responses to adaptive immunity, we discuss localized priming niches engineered to rescue dendritic cell cross-presentation. Furthermore, we examine interventions targeting T cell exhaustion-specifically metabolic checkpoint disruption, metalloimmunotherapy, and modalities that synchronize systemic mobilization with deep stromal infiltration. Finally, we review biomimetic and living-cell engineering strategies deployed to direct natural killer cells into the hypoxic tumor parenchyma. Despite robust preclinical data, clinical translation is fundamentally bottlenecked by the scalable manufacturing of complex nanomaterials, severe off-target neuroimmunological toxicities, and inherent physiological constraints of the host. Overcoming these hurdles demands structural minimalism and strict spatiotemporal precision. Ultimately, integrating synthetic biology with advanced 3D microfluidic models provides a necessary framework to bridge the gap between current preclinical achievements and future clinical viability.

title: Nanotherapeutic Strategies Targeting Senescent Microenvironment for Aging-Related Chronic Diseases.
abstract: DCellular senescence is a central driver of age-related chronic diseases, including neurodegeneration, atherosclerosis, metabolic disorders, and fibrosis. The persistent accumulation of senescent cells and their associated secretory phenotype (SASP) creates a shared microenvironmental basis for disease progression across multiple organ systems. Senolytic and senomorphic strategies targeting senescent cells have shown therapeutic promise, yet their clinical translation remains constrained by insufficient targeting specificity, off-target toxicity, and poor tissue penetration. Nanotechnology-enabled delivery systems offer a programmable approach to overcome these barriers through rationally designed carriers that enable selective recognition of senescent cells, microenvironment-responsive drug release, and enhanced tissue accessibility. This review develops an integrated framework that links nanoplatform design principles to mechanistic intervention categories and disease-specific evidence. We first outline the molecular basis of cellular senescence and its pathological roles in age-related diseases. We then systematically examine four mechanistic dimensions of nanotherapeutic intervention in the senescent microenvironment: redox homeostasis modulation, inflammatory reprogramming, senescent cell clearance, and immune surveillance reactivation. These dimensions target reactive oxygen species, pro-inflammatory cytokines, senescent cells, and immune effector cells, respectively. Representative nanoplatforms applied to neurodegenerative, cardiovascular, metabolic, musculoskeletal, and fibrotic diseases are discussed. We further analyze key translational challenges, including senescent cell heterogeneity, impaired drug delivery in aged tissues, and regulatory uncertainty. Finally, we discuss emerging directions in precision rejuvenation, offering a conceptual framework for the next generation of senescence-targeted nanotherapies.

title: Multimodal Assessment of the Effects of Acute Alcohol Intake on Resting-State Neural Function.
abstract: Combined neuroimaging modalities may clarify the mechanisms underlying alcohol's acute neurobehavioral effects. Past studies have typically focused on blood oxygen level-dependent (BOLD) correlates of alcohol-induced impairment. In this report, we integrated magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS), arterial spin labeling (ASL), and BOLD functional magnetic resonance imaging metrics to identify the mechanisms underlying acute alcohol effects on the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), given its critical role in attention, inhibition, and affect. Healthy social drinkers (n = 47; 49% women) received alcohol (target blood concentration: 0.08 g/dL) or placebo beverages during counterbalanced, double-blind sessions as part of a larger study. Thirty minutes later, ASL, resting-state BOLD, and single-voxel proton MRS spectra (30 mm isotropic) from the ACC were collected. Ethanol (EtOH) and glutamate (Glu) were quantified as ratio to the creatine (Cr) peak. Amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (ALFF) and whole-brain seed-voxel connectivity (clusterwise false discovery rate-corrected p [p FDR] .09). Alcohol increased the EtOH-to-Cr ratio (p < .001, d = 4.65) and Glu-to-Cr ratio (p = .002, d = 0.48), which were positively correlated (r = 0.30, p = .04). Alcohol reduced ACC ALFF (p = .018; d = 0.36) and perturbed its connectivity with the bilateral insula, paracingulate gyrus, inferior temporal gyrus, and opercular cortex (p FDR < .05). Changes in ACC Glu-to-Cr and EtOH-to-Cr ratios were accompanied by decreases in ALFF, which may suggest reduced functional capacity and perturbed connectivity with regions implicated in cognitive and affective function. Changes in CBF do not seem to underlie these effects. The results reflect the utility of multimodal imaging to identify mechanisms underlying the acute effects of alcohol and other drugs.

title: Loss of akt-1 throughout development leads to abnormal chemosensory behaviors in C. elegans.
abstract: The C. elegans AKT serine/threonine kinase AKT - 1 is widely studied because it is a molecular player in multiple ubiquitous signaling pathways. akt-1 mutants have been associated with gross, organismal-level phenotypes. In addition to organismal physiology, pathways associated with akt-1 are known to regulate neuronal plasticity and behavior; therefore, akt-1 mutants could be valuable for behavioral characterization. Here, we report that akt-1 loss-of-function mutants demonstrate perturbed chemotaxis behaviors which could confound experiments that rely on proper chemosensation. We also determined that adult-only administration of akt-1 RNAi is sufficient to overcome these behavioral deficits, suggesting these defects are likely developmental in origin.

title: MYCN-amplified spinal ependymoma: a three-patient case series and focussed literature review.
abstract: MYCN-amplified spinal ependymomas are a rare, recently described aggressive subtype of ependymoma defined by molecular profiling. We present three cases: a 52-year-old man, a 37-year-old woman, and a 28-year-old man presented with progressive neurological symptoms and spinal cord lesions identified on magnetic resonance imaging. These cases demonstrate the challenges in radiological identification and the importance of histological and molecular profiling to guide aggressive treatment of MYCN-amplified spinal ependymomas including surgical resection, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy. Outcomes varied across cases from clinical stability to death, reflecting the heterogeneity of the clinical course. We offer a short literature review to contextualise the cases.

title: European robin cryptochrome 4a does not bind 8-HDF or MTHF as second antenna chromophores.
abstract: Cryptochromes and photolyases are blue-light-sensitive flavoproteins that generally bind flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) and have distinct functions. Cryptochrome 4a (CRY4a) expressed in the double-cone photoreceptors of migratory songbirds such as the European robin (Erithacus rubecula) is the hypothesized primary sensor for avian magnetoreception. In addition to FAD, many photolyases and some cryptochromes bind antenna chromophores such as 8-hydroxy-5-deazaflavin (8-HDF) or 5,10-methenyltetrahydrofolate (MTHF). Here, we investigated whether Erithacus rubecula cryptochrome 4a (ErCRY4a) also binds 8-HDF and/or MTHF. 8-HDF binding was tested by co-expressing ErCRY4a with 8-HDF synthase. 8-HDF bound the positive control Xenopus laevis 6-4 photolyase (Xl6-4PL), but not ErCRY4a. For MTHF, the positive control Escherichia coli DNA photolyase (EcDPL) was purified with both MTHF and FAD, whereas ErCRY4a showed only FAD binding. Isothermal titration calorimetry also confirmed that MTHF does not bind ErCRY4a. Furthermore, computational analysis revealed no binding-site similarity between ErCRY4a and MTHF/8-HDF-binding proteins, indicating a non-conserved pocket.

title: A systematic review of case reports and case series of zolpidem in the diagnosis and treatment of catatonia.
abstract: Catatonia, commonly seen in psychiatric and medical practice, is often associated with increased morbidity and mortality. The neurotransmitter systems involved in catatonia include GABA, dopamine and glutamate. Benzodiazepines such as lorazepam, which act on GABA-A receptors, are used to confirm the diagnosis of catatonia, and are the mainstay of treatment. However, several patients with catatonia either don't respond to lorazepam or its use is not suitable or possible (e.g. due to supply issues). Zolpidem is a positive allosteric modulator of GABA-A receptors. There are an increasing number of case reports and one systematic review of its use in the diagnosis and treatment of catatonia. The objective of this systematic review is to explore the published evidence of zolpidem's efficacy as a diagnostic test and for treatment for catatonia. We systematically reviewed evidence for zolpidem use in diagnosis and/or treatment of catatonia, using the PRISMA guidelines. We identified 44 case reports and case series, with 79 patients who met the inclusion criteria through searches of PubMed, Medline, EMBASE, CINAHL, ProQuest and PsycInfo. 67 out of 79 patients (84.8%) with catatonia showed a positive response to zolpidem, with remission of catatonic symptoms in 24.1% of patients. The high response rate was evident regardless of its use as a challenge test (85.7%) or treatment (86.1%), either used alone (85.7%), or with a benzodiazepine (81.3%). The mean dose of zolpidem was 14.7mg, with a median of 10mg, and a range of 5 to 45mg, with a rapid mean time to response of 30.2 minutes. A few patients responded better to zolpidem at a higher dose and/or when used over a longer duration though this was not always the case. The response rate was higher in women (88.6%) as compared to men (64.7%). Although the results from this systematic review generate optimism for the use of zolpidem in diagnosis and treatment of catatonia, these results should be used with caution as there are no randomised controlled trials of zolpidem compared to placebo and/or lorazepam.

title: Neuropsychological evaluation and rehabilitation in multiple sclerosis (NEuRoMS): A mixed-methods, multi-centre feasibility randomised controlled trial.
journal: Multiple sclerosis journal - experimental, translational and clinical
abstract: Cognitive difficulties are common in people with multiple sclerosis (pwMS), yet access to neuropsychological rehabilitation is often limited or only provided to those with more severe impairments. The NEuRoMS intervention provides brief, tailored neuropsychological rehabilitation for pwMS with mild-to-moderate cognitive difficulties. To evaluate feasibility and acceptability of the intervention and test procedures for a definitive trial. A mixed-methods, multi-centre feasibility randomised controlled trial (RCT) was conducted. Feasibility outcomes were recruitment, retention, outcome completion, randomisation, intervention delivery and fidelity. Quantitative data were collected at baseline, 3- and 6-months, supplemented by interviews with pwMS and healthcare providers. Seventy-nine participants were randomised (mean age = 54.5 (SD = 11.5); 70% women) from three UK MS clinics. Most feasibility criteria were met: retention (>80%) and outcome-measure completion (81%-89%) were high, and trial procedures were acceptable. Intervention delivery was feasible and delivered as intended, but staffing-related recruitment challenges need addressing in future trials. Preliminary signal of efficacy was observed, with 3.42-point difference (effect size = 0.48) in the planned primary outcome (MS psychological impact) favouring the intervention, supported by qualitative evidence of sustained behaviour change. The NEuRoMS intervention and trial procedures were feasible and acceptable, with early indication of efficacy. A definitive RCT is underway.Trial registration: ISRCTN11203922; https://doi.org/10.1186/ISRCTN11203922.

title: Hippocampal tangential insertions of high-density silicon probes in head- fixed mice enhance spatial sampling.
abstract: The hippocampus is a key structure within the medial temporal lobe, which plays a central role in the formation and consolidation of declarative memories. Due to its complex croissant-like morphology, it has been difficult to use linear high-density probes to perform extracellular recordings from large continuous segments of the hippocampus. We here describe how to apply a tangential insertion approach to enable continuous recordings of the hippocampus. We propose two different insertions aligned to either the dorsal or ventral sections of the hippocampus. Both insertions are performed in head-fixed conditions, which can be easily combined with detailed monitoring of the animals' behavioral states. We show that when placed across the pyramidal layer, they can harness ripple oscillations at an unprecedented spatial resolution, which also enabled us to record up to 400 hippocampal neurons simultaneously from a single probe, endowing us with the capability to capture putative functionally connected neuronal pairs.

title: Deciphering the Anticancer Effects of Baicalein in Human Gastric Cancer Cells: Computational Chemistry, Bioinformatics, Network Pharmacology Insights, and in vitro Experimental Validation.
journal: Iranian journal of pharmaceutical research : IJPR
abstract: Baicalein, a natural flavone, exhibits multifaceted anticancer potential; however, its molecular mechanisms in gastric carcinoma remain unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms of baicalein in human gastric cancer (GC) using an integrated approach combining computational chemistry, network pharmacology, bioinformatics, and in vitro assays. Network pharmacology and bioinformatics analyses were conducted to identify hub targets and enriched signaling pathways of baicalein in GC. Molecular docking was then performed to evaluate binding affinities for key proteins, including AKT1, STAT3, and mutant TP53. These in silico findings informed subsequent in vitro validation. The primary outcome was cell viability, assessed by the MTT assay; secondary outcomes included apoptosis, assessed by flow cytometry, and changes in protein expression, assessed by Western blotting. Density functional theory (DFT) analysis indicated favorable electronic properties of baicalein, with a HOMO-LUMO gap of 3.787 eV, and demonstrated similarity to reference inhibitors targeting mutant TP53, AKT, and STAT3. SwissADME indicated drug-likeness, with no rule violations, a bioavailability of 0.55, high gastrointestinal absorption, and blood-brain barrier permeability. Network pharmacology identified 382 targets. Overlap with 1,001 GC genes yielded 181 common targets, forming a significant protein-protein interaction network with 181 nodes and 641 edges and identifying TP53, AKT1, and STAT3 as hubs. The analysis suggested that baicalein may act as a multitarget modulator affecting the PI3K-Akt, MAPK, and apoptosis pathways. In vitro validation supported these predictions. The MTT assay showed selective, dose-dependent cytotoxicity, with IC50 values of 40.25 μM in SGC-7901 cells and 77.95 μM in GES-1 cells. Microscopy confirmed apoptotic morphology, flow cytometry showed increased Annexin V-positive cells consistent with intrinsic apoptosis, and Western blotting revealed downregulation of AKT1 and STAT3 with slight upregulation of mutant TP53, supporting their roles in carcinogenesis. Baicalein may exert selective anticancer effects in GC through multitarget modulation of the PI3K-Akt, MAPK, and apoptosis pathways, particularly via AKT1, STAT3, and mutant TP53. These findings support its potential as a therapeutic candidate, pending further validation.

title: Specificity of non-motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Middle-aged and older adults (>55 years old) have a high risk of developing Parkinson's disease (PD); however, many non-motor symptoms (NMSs) indicative of PD are also common in middle-aged and older adults without a neurological disease diagnosis. To identify symptoms specific to PD in comparison to controls without a neurological disease diagnosis. This is a systematic review and meta-analysis. We performed a meta-analysis, using Embase, SciSearch, MEDLINE, and BIOSIS from January 1, 2001, until April 1, 2025. We included observational studies reporting the prevalence of NMSs using the non-motor symptom questionnaire or non-motor symptom scale in the PD population versus controls. Using a random effects model, we generated a pooled estimate for the prevalence risk ratio (RR) for each symptom. The meta-analyses included 15 studies, involving 7393 PD patients and 2742 controls. It showed 28 out of 30 NMSs were more common in the PD population, with excessive drooling (RR = 7.30 (95% confidence interval; CI 5.05-10.57)), visual hallucinations (RR = 6.48 (95% CI 3.61-11.64)) and taste/smell issues (RR = 4.67 (95% CI 3.07-7.10)) being the most specific symptoms (having the largest RRs). Planning screening campaigns to identify PD among middle-aged and older adults is difficult, due to the high numbers that are needed to screen using tools that are not specific enough. We showed that excessive drooling and taste/smell issues are highly specific NMSs of PD, as they have high RRs. More research is needed to assess their usefulness to be included as an enrichment factor in screening campaigns for PD patients in a middle-aged and older adult population.

title: Choroid Plexus Papilloma Mimicking Chiari II Malformation in an Infant With Myelomeningocele: A Case Report.
abstract: We describe a rare case of an infant with a diagnostic conundrum of apnoeic episodes, on the background of antenatally diagnosed myelomeningocele and Chiari II malformation (CM2). The infant underwent extensive neurosurgical interventions in the first few weeks of life and treatment including foramen magnum decompression of CM2 and placement of a ventriculoperitoneal shunt for hydrocephalus, with an incidental finding of a choroid plexus papilloma (CPP) WHO Grade 1. The apnoeic episodes persisted and required multidisciplinary discussion, considering the relative likelihood of competing aetiologies. Investigations eventually led to the finding that urinary tract infection was exacerbating the apnoeic episodes and may have contributed to the frequency or severity of the apnoeic episodes. From a neurosurgical perspective, we discuss whether CM2, the fourth-ventricular CPP, and associated hydrocephalus may have contributed to brainstem dysfunction and respiratory dysregulation. From a neurosurgical perspective, we discuss the potential contributions of CM2, a fourth-ventricular CPP, hydrocephalus, and brainstem dysfunction to the infant's respiratory events. The temporal association between urinary tract infection and increased apnoeic episodes also raises the possibility of bladder-mediated autonomic dysregulation, although a single definitive aetiology was not established.

title: High-Risk Screening for Late-Onset Pompe Disease in Northern China: Prevalence, Genotypic Spectrum, and Diagnostic Challenges.
abstract: Late-onset Pompe disease (LOPD), also known as late-onset glycogen storage disease Type II, is caused by a genetic deficiency of the lysosomal enzyme acid α-glucosidase (GAA). LOPD typically results in progressive weakness of the limb-girdle and respiratory muscles and is often accompanied by the involvement of other systems, such as skeleton, smooth muscle, and the cerebrovascular system. The incidence of LOPD in China remains unknown, underscoring the need for large-scale epidemiological studies to better characterize the clinical spectrum. This prospective, multicenter, observational cohort study was conducted across 39 neurology centers in 12 northern Chinese provinces. A novel pragmatic approach was utilized, which included the development and application of a standardized high-risk profile for LOPD suspicion, derived from collective diagnostic and therapeutic experience throughout the region. Individuals meeting 2 or more criteria in this predefined high-risk profile were enrolled. Subsequent screening involved initial analysis of GAA enzyme activity using dried blood spot (DBS) testing and patients with deficient enzyme activity underwent confirmatory genetic testing to establish a definitive LOPD diagnosis. Between January 2022 and December 2024, 1878 high-risk patients were enrolled. Screening identified 46 patients (2.45%) diagnosed with LOPD based on DBS analysis and subsequent genetic confirmation. This study demonstrates a significant prevalence of LOPD among a clinically high-risk population in Northern China. These findings underscore the critical importance of targeted screening programs for early identification. Early diagnosis enables timely initiation of enzyme replacement therapy (ERT), which can significantly mitigate the disease course, improve quality of life, and reduce long-term healthcare burden.

title: Oviductus Ranae Protein Hydrolysate (ORPH) Ameliorates CUMS-Induced Depressive-Like Behaviors in Mice via Modulation of Gut Microbiota and Metabolic Signatures: An Integrated Multi-Omics Investigation.
abstract: Depression constitutes a significant global health burden, manifesting as persistent low mood, anhedonia, and behavioral disturbances. The pathogenesis of depression is multifactorial, involving hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis dysregulation, monoaminergic neurotransmitter abnormalities, and neuroinflammatory processes. Oviductus Ranae protein hydrolysate (ORPH) is an enzymatically hydrolysed extract derived from the dried oviducts of female Rana dybowskii Günther (Oviductus Ranae, OR). This esteemed traditional Chinese medicine, indigenous to Northeast China, has been utilized as a valuable tonic for centuries. Previous in vivo investigations have demonstrated the anti-neuroinflammatory effects of OR. Chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) is widely used to establish a mouse model of depressive-like phenotypes. This study aimed to investigate whether ORPH could alleviate CUMS-induced depressive-like behaviors in mice and explore its underlying mechanisms from the perspective of gut microbiota and metabolic profiles. A CUMS paradigm was employed to establish a murine model of depression, and the effects of 0.2, 0.4, or 0.8 g/kg ORPH on depressive-like behaviors were systematically evaluated. Biochemical analyses were conducted to quantify inflammatory mediators, neurotransmitters, and HPA axis-associated hormones in murine serum and brain tissue. Multi-omics approaches, encompassing brain tissue metabolomics, fecal metabolomics, and gut microbiota sequencing, were utilized to elucidate key metabolic constituents and signaling pathways implicated in the regulation of cerebral and gut microbial communities. In vivo experiments were conducted to investigate the effects of microbiota depletion and blockade of key metabolites on the therapeutic efficacy of ORPH. Administration of ORPH at doses of 0.2, 0.4, or 0.8 g/kg markedly ameliorated depressive-like behaviors in CUMS-exposed mice. ORPH increased the sucrose preference rate, reduced immobility time in the FST and TST, and shortened the escape latency in the MWM of CUMS mice. Biochemical assays revealed that ORPH attenuated serum and cerebral concentrations of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-1β, and TNF-α), reduced circulating ACTH and CRH levels, decreased cerebral CORT content, and elevated cerebral 5-HT and NE levels. Moreover, ORPH significantly mitigated hippocampal tissue injury and apoptosis. Metabolomic analyses identified therapeutic modulation of pathways such as sphingolipid and tryptophan metabolism, while gut microbiota profiling highlighted the enrichment of these taxa, including Lactobacillus. The protective effect of ORPH was obviously weakened after microbiota depletion, and similar attenuation was observed upon inhibiting tryptophan hydroxylase (TPH) activity and sphingosine kinase (SphK). These findings indicate that ORPH may exert favorable therapeutic potential against CUMS-induced depressive-like phenotypes, possibly through modulation of dysregulated sphingolipid and tryptophan metabolism, which could contribute to the alleviation of neuroinflammation linked to gut microbiota dysbiosis.

title: Unlocking Colorectal Cancer Diagnostics With Circulating Progastrin (hPG80): A Scoping Review.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) represents a significant global health concern, ranking as the third most diagnosed cancer and the second leading cause of cancer deaths in the UK. Although population-based bowel cancer screening programs (BCSP) facilitate early diagnosis, uptake remains variable. Blood-based biomarkers, such as human progastrin 80 (hPG80), offer a patient-friendly approach to enhance screening compliance and clinical management. This scoping review, conducted according to PRISMA-ScR guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420250654595), searched Ovid Medline/PubMed, Ovid Embase, and Cochrane databases from January 1990 to January 2025. Studies assessing plasma hPG80 as a CRC biomarker were included, while reviews, in vitro studies, and animal models were excluded. Quality assessment was performed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and findings were synthesized narratively. Five articles encompassing 2,692 participants met the inclusion criteria. The included studies consistently demonstrated significant overexpression of hPG80 in CRC patients compared to non-cancer controls, with an increased median progastrin concentration in the CRC group (27.5 pmol/L) compared to patients with polyps or normal controls. Furthermore, hPG80 levels decreased significantly post-surgery (from 272.3 ± 12.0 pmol/L to 161.3 ± 11.0 pmol/L), reflecting its sensitivity to tumor burden and potential for treatment monitoring. Methodologically, literature has shifted from early radioimmunoassays to safer, cost-effective enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISA). A meta-analysis was not feasible due to variations in analytes, assays, populations, thresholds, and a lack of CRC-specific sensitivity, specificity, or area under the curve data. This review highlights hPG80's promise as a reliable, reproducible blood-based biomarker for CRC integration into BCSPs and symptomatic pathways. However, optimal thresholds, stage-specific correlation, molecular subtypes, and cost-effectiveness remain unanswered. The ongoing MOTION trial (NCT07035691) is currently evaluating hPG80's performance within UK symptomatic suspected colorectal cancer referral pathways.

title: Emerging digital technologies to improve health outcomes in people with intellectual disability: A scoping review.
abstract: People with intellectual disability experience higher rates of multi-morbidity, preventable deaths, and barriers to healthcare access compared to the general population. Emerging digital technologies may address these disparities, but evidence examining their application, effectiveness, and feasibility for people with intellectual disability remains fragmented across multiple disciplines. To examine applications of emerging digital technologies for health outcomes in people with intellectual disability across health domains over the past decade. Scoping review conducted following Joanna Briggs Institute guidelines. Systematic searches were conducted across PsycINFO, PubMed, and IEEE Xplore in June 2025. Studies were included if they reported on emerging digital technologies (excluding telehealth) supporting health outcomes for people with intellectual disability, presented quantitative or qualitative data, and were published from 2015-2025. Thirty-six studies were included, spanning seven health domains. Physical activity and motor skills were the most frequently addressed domains, whilst healthcare access and mental health remained underexplored. Technologies included gaming consoles, head-mounted displays, mobile applications, and augmented and mixed reality technology. Most interventions reported improvements in primary outcomes including physical fitness, balance, anxiety reduction, and skill acquisition. Emerging digital technologies demonstrate feasibility and safety for people with intellectual disability across multiple health domains. To date, research has focused on physical health using consumer technologies. Future research should expand to healthcare access and mental health interventions, involve people with intellectual disability in co-design, and demonstrate pathways to independent use in home and community settings to address documented health disparities.

title: Prevalence and clinical correlates of obsessive-compulsive disorder in central nervous system autoimmune demyelinating diseases: A cross-sectional observational Study.
abstract: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is a disabling psychiatric comorbidity that may be underrecognized in multiple sclerosis (MS) and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD). Evidence regarding its prevalence and associated factors in these populations remains limited. To estimate the prevalence of OCD and examine its clinical and demographic correlates in patients with MS and NMOSD in an Iranian cohort. Cross-sectional observational study. This cross-sectional study (January 2018-December 2024) included patients with MS and NMOSD from Kashani Hospital and Hakim MS Clinic, Isfahan, Iran. MS and NMOSD diagnoses were made according to the 2017 McDonald and 2015 IPND criteria, respectively. OCD was diagnosed by certified psychiatrists per DSM-IV. Demographic, clinical, and neuropsychological data were extracted from interviews and medical records. Group comparisons were performed using t-tests or χ2 tests, followed by univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses. Of 4,759 patients (mean age, 42.9 years; 77.1% female), 4,460 had MS (3,502 with relapsing-remitting MS (RRMS), 212 with primary progressive MS (PPMS), and 746 with secondary progressive MS (SPMS)), and 299 had NMOSD. OCD prevalence was 15.4% in MS, highest in RRMS (17.8%), and 12.7% in NMOSD. Across all participants, female sex (OR 1.32, 95% CI 1.04-1.64), higher educational attainment, sensory vs. motor onset symptoms, migraine (OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.16-1.83), and hypothyroidism (OR 1.29, 95% CI 1.01-1.65), lower EDSS (OR per 1-unit: 0.78, 95% CI 0.70 - 0.88), and shorter disease duration (OR per 1-year: 0.98, 95% CI 0.97 - 1.00) were significantly associated with higher odds of OCD. OCD is frequently observed among patients with MS and NMOSD and shows distinct clinical associations, including migraine, hypothyroidism, sensory onset phenotype, and lower disability. Recognition of psychiatric comorbidities in these disorders may facilitate more comprehensive and individualized clinical management.

title: Micronutrients and tension-type headache: A case-control study on intake and blood levels.
abstract: Tension-type headache (TTH) is the most common form of primary headache, in which diet plays a key role as a modifiable lifestyle component. This study aimed to assess the levels of micronutrients in individuals with TTH compared to healthy participants. This population-based case-control study was conducted using data from the Isfahan Functional Disorders longitudinal cohort study. The cohort consisted of 1943 adults aged 18-65 years, randomly selected between September 2017 and March 2018. Participants with TTH were clinically diagnosed according to the International Classification of Headache Disorders III criteria by trained physicians, and a control group was defined as individuals without any diagnosed primary headache disorder. Dietary intake was assessed using a food frequency questionnaire, validated for the Iranian population, and serum levels of certain micronutrients were measured. Out of 1638 participants who completed dietary and headache-related information, 1072 were diagnosed with TTH, with 596 classified as infrequent TTH (iTTH), 425 as frequent TTH (fTTH), and 65 as chronic TTH (cTTH). Individuals with TTH had higher intakes of vitamin B6 and vitamin K, lower serum magnesium levels, and higher serum vitamin D levels compared to healthy controls. Additionally, participants with cTTH had higher dietary intake of folate, biotin, potassium, magnesium, molybdenum, and serum levels of vitamin D compared to those with iTTH. This study underscores the higher intake of vitamin B6 and vitamin K among subjects with TTH, along with lower serum magnesium levels and higher serum vitamin D levels. Further longitudinal studies are needed to explore these associations and develop effective interventions for TTH.

title: Plasma biomarker signatures in patients with rapidly progressive dementia.
abstract: Overlapping clinical features and results of common diagnostic tests confound early, accurate recognition of distinct causes of rapidly progressive dementia (RPD). Objective, accessible tools are needed to improve etiologic diagnoses and inform counseling and treatment decisions. Biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease neuropathology, neuroaxonal injury, neuroinflammation, vascular injury, metabolic dysfunction, and systemic inflammation were measured in plasma from 58 patients with RPD and 40 patients with typically progressive neurodegenerative diseases enrolled in prospective studies of memory and aging. Neuroaxonal injury and neuroinflammation biomarkers were elevated in patients with prion and vascular (versus other) causes of RPD. Markers of systemic inflammation were uniquely elevated in patients with rapidly versus typically progressive neurodegenerative diseases. Higher phosphorylated tau (p-tau)217 and p-tau181 levels, and lower amyloid beta 42/40 levels, were nominally associated with treatment-non-responsive causes of RPD. Blood biomarkers may inform biological heterogeneity underlying RPD with potential diagnostic and therapeutic implications pending validation in larger longitudinal cohorts.

title: In vitro study of selenomethionine's concentration-dependent effects in a 6-OHDA model of Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by oxidative stress-induced degeneration of dopaminergic neurons. This study evaluated the concentration-related neuroprotective effects of Selenomethionine (SeMet) against 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA)- induced toxicity using an in vitro model of N27 dopaminergic cells. In vitro models provide an essential platform for identifying therapeutic candidates and elucidating cellular mechanisms before validation in animal models. N27 cells were pretreated with SeMet (2, 10, or 30 µM) followed by 30 µM 6-OHDA exposure. Intracellular glutathione (GSH) and ascorbic acid levels were quantified. Cell viability was assessed using the Trypan blue exclusion assay. Protein content and morphology were evaluated via Coomassie staining and ImageJ-based morphometric analysis. 6-OHDA significantly reduced GSH (0.0044 ± 0.0005 µM) and ascorbic acid (3.28 ± 0.55 µM) compared to control. Pretreatment with 30 µM SeMet significantly restored GSH (0.0330 ± 0.0076 µM; p < 0.01*) and ascorbic acid (4.59 ± 0.93 µM; p < 0.05*). Cell viability declined to 44.0 ± 2.34% with 6-OHDA but improved significantly with 30 µM SeMet co-treatment (81.3 ± 9.82%; p < 0.001***), although 10 µM was found to be the most effective overall, consistent with the biphasic concentration response of selenium compounds. Protein content dropped to 8.05 ± 4.50 AU with 6-OHDA and recovered with SeMet (70.21 ± 24.59 AU). Integrated density analysis and morphology confirmed cellular protection. These in vitro findings demonstrate that SeMet exerts concentration-dependent neuroprotective effects against 6-OHDA-induced oxidative stress in N27 cells. The highest concentration of SeMet (30 µM) offered optimal protection, supporting SeMet's therapeutic potential for early-stage PD intervention strategies.

title: Decoding the implicit paradigm of exosome targeting blood brain barrier in neurodegenerative diseases: Molecular insight and therapeutic perspective.
abstract: Exosome physiology in the progression of neurodegenerative diseases is intricately tangled with various protein aggregations, including tau protein, α-synuclein, and amyloid-β protein. Exosomes facilitate therapeutic and prognostic avenues through cell-to-cell crosstalk mechanisms, drug delivery, and biomarker isolation strategies in neurodegenerative disease management. The significant implications of molecular insights into neurofibrillary tangles and synaptic dysfunction have been extensively explored through microRNA (miRNA) regulation. The therapeutic potential of exosomes as nano-cargo systems is significant in nervous tissue regeneration and the treatment of neuronal lesions. Advancements in exosome engineering, including genetic modifications, have expanded their capacity to transport RNA molecules, proteins, and novel gene-editing tools such as CRISPR/Cas9, thereby enabling neuroprotective treatment protocols. Integration with immunotherapeutic approaches further highlights exosomes as promising components of combined strategies with important clinical outcomes.

title: Patterns of Intravenous Buprenorphine-Naloxone Misuse: Psychiatric Morbidity, Risk Behaviours, Diversion, and Serological Findings.
abstract: Intravenous misuse of buprenorphine-naloxone (BPNX) is a growing concern for patients with opioid use disorder (OUD). However, data on psychiatric comorbidities, patterns of diversion, and the burden of infectious diseases among individuals who inject BPNX in India remain limited. This study aimed to assess the clinical profile, diversion patterns, and seroprevalence among these patients. Seventy-three patients with a diagnosis of OUD injecting BPNX, were recruited for this study. Sociodemographic and clinical variables, diversion patterns, high-risk behaviors, and overdose history were assessed using a semi-structured proforma. Triple serology testing for HIV, HBV, and HCV was conducted, and relevant statistical analyses were performed. The participants were predominantly young men with a mean age of 25.9 ± 6.05 years. Psychiatric comorbidity was present in 67.1% of participants, and attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) was the most common diagnosis. HCV seropositivity was found in 68.5% and HCV RNA in 52.05%. Most participants used both prescription and diverted BPNX to avoid withdrawal symptoms. High-frequency misuse was significantly linked to longer opioid dependence and needle sharing. The misuse of intravenous BPNX was linked to significant psychiatric comorbidity, unsafe injection practices, and a high burden of infectious diseases. The persistence of diversion despite the BPNX combination formulation suggests the current naloxone dose ratio may not be effective as a deterrent. Urgent integrated addiction, psychiatric, and harm-reduction services are needed.

title: End-to-end deep learning for identifying Alzheimer's disease signatures in spectral fluorescence imaging of normal-appearing brain regions in 5xFAD mice.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the leading cause of dementia, characterized by the accumulation of amyloid- β and tau aggregates in the brain. Current diagnostic approaches primarily detect mature plaques, but growing evidence suggests that pre-fibrillar aggregates are present earlier in normal-appearing tissue and may provide a valuable window for intervention. We propose the first proof-of-concept end-to-end deep learning (DL) model to identify AD signatures directly from normal-appearing tissue (i.e., background parenchyma) of raw spectral fluorescence data. To develop and evaluate our DL model, we used one million signals extracted from spectral fluorescence images of brain cortex sections collected from wild-type and 5xFAD mice (a transgenic strain carrying five familial human AD mutations). Our results demonstrate that AD-related signatures can indeed be detected in normal-appearing brain cortex regions. Experiments revealed that model performance depends on input dimensions, training set size, and the preprocessing kernel size. The optimal configuration used 1000 × 32 input, 9000 training samples, and a 3 × 3 kernel, achieving ≥ 95 % accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F 1 -score, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. Importantly, no mice were misclassified, and saliency analysis indicated that a broad range of spectral fluorescence wavelengths contributed to the model's decisions. These findings highlight the potential of DL-based analysis of spectral fluorescence data to enable earlier detection of AD-related changes, supporting a shift toward a more proactive strategy for biomarker discovery.

title: Beyond Seizure Control: Building the Infrastructure for Disease-Modifying Therapies in Epilepsy.
abstract: Rapid advances in disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) for epilepsy, including gene-based therapies, antisense oligonucleotides, and stem cell-derived approaches, are reshaping the treatment landscape. As these therapies move through clinical trials and toward regulatory review, they introduce complex clinical, operational, ethical, and equity considerations that extend well beyond traditional antiseizure medication management. Successful integration will require careful attention to patient selection, genetic and biomarker testing, multidisciplinary care models, infrastructure readiness, referral pathways, long-term safety monitoring, informed consent for novel and potentially irreversible interventions, access to clinical trials, and cost and reimbursement challenges. Significant investments in personnel, systems, and facilities may be necessary, raising important questions about implementation across diverse practice settings and the risk of widening disparities in care. Here, we review the evolving therapeutic pipeline and outline key considerations for safe, ethical, and equitable implementation.

title: Accuracy of different methods for predicting proximity to failure during resistance training.
abstract: Proximity to failure (PTF) is increasingly considered in resistance training (RT). Two common methods used to prescribe PTF are rating of perceived exertion (RPE) and repetitions in reserve (RIR). This study compared the accuracy of RIR and RPE for predicting PTF. In a randomised crossover design, 32 participants (19 trained, 13 untrained) completed machine chest press and leg extension exercises at 75% of one-repetition maximum. Participants completed two experimental sessions, one using RIR and one using Borg-RPE. Experimental session (RIR/RPE) and exercise order were randomised. During each set, participants indicated when they believed they had reached 2 RIR or 8 RPE and then continued to momentary failure. Accuracy was calculated as the difference between actual repetitions remaining to failure and the number predicted at the verbal call. No significant differences in accuracy were observed between RIR and Borg-RPE for either exercise (chest press: mean difference -0.03 repetitions, 95% CI - 0.50 to 0.44, p = 0.893; leg extension: mean difference 0.16 repetitions, 95% CI - 0.39 to 0.71, p = 0.556). Training status did not influence the difference in accuracy between methods. These findings indicate that Borg-RPE and RIR produce similar accuracy when estimating PTF during machine-based RT under the conditions tested.

title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists in adults with overweight/obesity and alcohol use disorder: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Emerging evidence suggests glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) may improve outcomes in alcohol use disorder (AUD), which is associated with cardiovascular risk and mortality. Evaluate the association between initiation of GLP-1RAs and clinical outcomes among adults with AUD and overweight or obesity. A retrospective cohort study using electronic health records from TriNetX research network, with participants enrolled between January 1, 2015 and December 31, 2024 and followed through December 31, 2025. Inverse probability of treatment weighting, based on propensity scores, balanced baseline characteristics. Weighted logistic regression models estimated the adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) at 1-year follow-up. Adults ≥18 years old with overweight or obesity and AUD, without prior GLP-1RAs, or cancer or non-nicotine substance use disorder diagnoses. At least one GLP-1RA prescription issued after enrollment (Treatment cohort); none for Controls. Presence (Yes/No) of all-cause and alcohol-related hospitalizations, mortality, and major cardiovascular events (MCVE) since the GLP-1RA initiation (Treatment cohort) or post-enrollment (Control cohort).
